News.title: Burnham needs to stop trying to be cool… people want a PM who tackles big issues rather than shares Spotify playlists
News.content:
SHOULD politicians ever try to be cool? Our political leaders certainly seem to think so.

Andy Burnham is all about the cool, Northern vibes.



He has a dedicated teenage TikTok fandom that helped propel him to No10 by splicing together video footage of the new PM set to bubblegum pop songs.

He danced on stage to New Order’s True Faith when he was crowned Labour leader.



Burnham even took the odd day off ­politics to DJ at clubs in Manchester’s trendy Northern Quarter (although this was when he was Greater Manchester Mayor — not PM).

Britain’s new Prime Minister is — we are told — “lit, rizz, dank”.



And he is not the only politician on a mission to show he is cool.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski is more likely to be seen on stage at a rave than being interviewed on the Six O’Clock News.

Even Reform’s Nigel Farage is all about the ­TikTok likes, with 1.5million followers on the platform.

Increasingly, it feels like politics is just a vibe — and we are being asked to drink the Kool-Aid.



On the one hand, there is nothing ­particularly new about politicians trying to be a bit hip.

Remember Tony Blair having Noel ­Gallagher and a bunch of artists round for beers at No10 as he rode the Cool ­Britannia wave? Or Gordon Brown saying he liked the Arctic ­Monkeys?

But then that proves my point — there is a fine line between cool and cringe.

As one veteran Labour MP said to me the other day, “The thing is — us ­politicians just aren’t cool.”



And there’s the rub.

Our political class are, by definition, the men and women in grey suits.

The public wants to see them hard at work fixing the NHS and stopping the small boats — not spinning discs on a stage in Ibiza.

Maybe some of our politicians used to be cool, way back when at university, when they had long, floppy hair, were in a band and wrote tortured poetry for their girlfriends.



But those are faded memories.

Once they cut off their locks, put on an M&S suit and took their first political internship they stopped being cool.

Instead, they stepped into a world of opening school fetes, judging the biggest marrow competition and shoving leaflets in people’s ­letterboxes.

It is important and often unglamorous work. But it is not cool.

Burnham became a ­parliamentary researcher for Labour MP Tessa Jowell when he was 24.



His life may have been a hedonistic whirlwind before — I really don’t know. But from that day on he joined the grind of politics.

Don’t get me wrong, politicians can and should be relatable. Even charismatic, if they can manage it.

They need to pass the “would I want to go for a pint with them?” test.

Farage and Burnham do. Turns out Keir Starmer didn’t — and that’s why he isn’t Prime Minister any more.

As countless Labour MPs tell me, ­Burnham just has better vibes.



But a word of warning to the new PM — cool vibes don’t last.

The British public want politicians who can run the economy, improve the NHS, and stop the small boats crisis.

They don’t really care what is on your Spotify jogging playlist or what your favourite IPA is.

And they don’t want to see you dancing in a club when the economy is in the ­doldrums and taxes are sky high.

Every time the Green Party throws a rave, it makes itself a little less electable and a little bit more fringe.



So, yes Andy, flutter those dark eyelashes at the TikTok camera as you pull a pint and tuck in to some scampi fries down the pub.

Incidentally, I love scampi fries and am always up for a TikTok collab.

But don’t chase the cool too hard. Listen to New Order at home and fix the boats crisis in public.

Then the voters will really rate you.

GREEN ZOE’S SHAMEFUL ‘ERROR’



A GREEN Party mayor wants to end her ­council’s link to Israel – on the third anniversary of the Hamas terror attacks.

Zoe Garbett, Mayor of Hackney in East London, has written to the city of Haifa in Israel saying she wants to end the twinning relationship and demanding a response by October 7.

This sounds like a sick joke. Unfortunately, it isn’t. October 7, 2023, was the date Hamas launched its bloody attacks on Israel.

Nearly 1,200 people were murdered, while thousands more were injured or kidnapped and held hostage.

It was the deadliest attack on Jews since the Holocaust.



Let that sink in.

Imagine choosing that date?

Garbett has apologised, describing it as an “oversight”, but surely no one is thick enough to pick it by ­mistake?

Regardless, what an insult to a country whose people were slaughtered by a Jew-hating ­terror group.

It is shameful.



FOR 70 years the Lovell ­Telescope has stood proudly in Cheshire – mapping galaxies far away and protecting us from the Soviets during the Cold War.

But now it is under threat and could close because of funding cuts.

Scientists are up in arms at the news, saying it damages the UK’s global reputation for research.

UK Research and Innovation has cut annual funding to Jodrell Bank, which houses the telescope, inset, by £2.8million, and now it is in a race against time to find the money to plug the shortfall.



Britain is a giant of science. We are the ­country of Isaac Newton, Charles Darwin and Stephen Hawking. We must not risk losing this reputation. The bureaucrats need to rethink the cuts.

BRITAIN is burning. Europe has been ablaze with wildfires for weeks, and now one has broken out in Suffolk.

The UK’s climate is changing. We are getting hotter and wetter, so why are we not building more reservoirs? Britain has not built a reservoir since 1992. That is nearly 35 years ago.

Our politicians are only too happy to set pie-in-the-sky Net Zero goals and spend billions buying solar panels from China.



But they can’t get their act together to build a single reservoir, which could be used to store water and put out a wildfire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is a dereliction of duty that shames every one of our political class. So, enough hot air about Net Zero.

Get on and do the day job – build the ­infrastructure we need.

News.title: ‘Intimidating’ female sailor who sexually assaulted 4 shipmates on Royal Navy warship to ‘dominate’ them is jailed
News.content:
NAVY ABUSE ‘Intimidating’ female sailor who sexually assaulted 4 shipmates on Royal Navy warship to ‘dominate’ them is jailed

A FEMALE sailor who sexually assaulted male and female colleagues while aboard a Royal Navy destroyer has been jailed.

Able Seaman Sian Dowsett, 25, was booted out the Navy after being found guilty of abusing four colleagues in a “disgraceful” campaign of intimidation.



Dowsett was branded a “predator” by a military judge who heard how she targeted both male and and female colleagues.

The court learned that Dowsett – who had “bisexual tendencies” – would “target new members” on board Type 45 destroyer HMS Dauntless.



She reportedly grabbed the male sailors by their crotches and stroked their arms on multiple occasions.

The suspect also allegedly made vastly inappropriate comments like, “I like my coffee how I like my men, big and strong”.

To make matters worse, she smacked female sailors’ bums and squeezed their breasts, saying, “Do you like that baby girl?”

A court martial earlier this year heard Dowsett took advantage of new recruits who she thought would not report her.



During the torrid proceedings, Dowsett was said to be a “cancer on the ship”.

One of her victims described the “embarrassment” of being molested by a woman of lower rank than her.

“I shared a mess with her and I couldn’t talk about the incident because she would hear,” the victim said.

“I was also embarrassed – not only that I had been sexually assaulted by a woman but a woman who was of a lower rank than me and who should look up to me.”

“She was an extremely intimidating character. She would scream and shout at people.



“I had so many sleepless nights when she was aboard. She had unrestricted access to me and I honestly believed she would physically attack me.

“I thought if she knew I reported it her anger would have been uncontrollable.”

One of her male victims told Bulford Military Court in Wiltshire how he was left feeling “anxious” after the harrowing ordeal.

“I felt guilty that I let it happen but I didn’t tell her to get off. I was assaulted again in the hangar,” he said.

“She did this to me in front of two males I work with which made me feel embarrassed. I stood there in disbelief.”



On top of the hefty jail sentence, she was dismissed from the Navy over six convictions for sexual assault.

Dowsett had reportedly been recently diagnosed with autism, which could cause “social exploitation, interpersonal misunderstanding and difficulty navigating social and institutional environments”.

Assistant Judge John Atwill said that these were “acts that any person would know are unacceptable”.

Sentencing Dowsett, the judge said: “Service personnel have little choice over who they work and live with. The confines of work in ships brings them into close proximity with work colleagues.

“The use of that proximity to abuse and dominate others violates their autonomy and drives division into the teams in which they work.



“Your behaviour towards them was disgraceful. You upset, frightened and disconcerted them and you had no regard for the impact of your behaviour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You were a predator in that ship, and seemed to target newer members.”

Dowsett joined the navy in 2019 and was serving as a chef aboard HMS Dauntless at the time of the offences.

News.title: Aunt of Brit woman found stuffed in suitcase pays tribute to ‘beautiful’ niece & says ‘we can’t believe this happened’
News.content:
THE aunt of a Brit woman found dead inside a suitcase has paid tribute to her “beautiful” niece and says: “we can’t believe this happened”.

Elisabeth Ross, known as Lisa, was discovered inside a suitcase by a homeless man in Athens on July 18, sparking a major police probe.



The 38-year-old was last seen leaving her friend’s house three days earlier on her way to see some American pals in the Kypseli district.

Cops tracing her final movements have said the Brit’s phone was switched on and being used in the days after she died.



They believe that messages were sent in an apparent attempt to mislead those who might have been trying to get in touch with her.

Her heartbroken dad revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her mysterious death.



The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek police he was sent several messages for two weeks after Lisa’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.

Her aunt, Anne Bangham, has paid a touching tribute to her “beautiful loving” niece.

She wrote: “We just can’t believe it she was such a beautiful loving and kind young lady.

I wish I could get my hands on whoever did it. She had not long arrived there to work.



“It will take a while to sink in… We are absolutely devastated.”

Another woman wrote: “RIP beautiful Lisa. I will always remember you for your beautiful smile, warmth, care and kindness you showed to everyone.”

Lisa is believed to have travelled to Greece from the US for work via her hometown of Edinburgh.



She was reportedly staying at a friend’s house in Attica for several weeks before she was last seen on July 15.

Cops are desperate to uncover what happened to Elisabeth during the three days she is unaccounted for.

The homeless man who found her has insisted that the suitcase was not in the derelict building on July 16 and July 17.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.

They are now combing the area for security cameras that might have captured the suitcase dump.



Local hotels and residences are also being examined, with police speculating that the body was likely taken to the building from close quarters.

Police spokesperson Konstantia Dimoglidou told The Sun: “The key to this case is to find out what happened to the woman during those three days as we don’t know anything about her moves on the 15th, 16th and 17th.

“The main focus is to find her cause of death as the medical examiner did not find any signs of struggle or injury on her body.

“We are waiting for the toxicology reports to shed some light in the next few days.

“We cannot be talking about a murder if we don’t know what happened to her – maybe she died and someone tried to hide her body, anything is possible and at this point it’s too soon to tell.



“As part of the investigation we are also checking CCTV from the area where she was found and we are working to trace her phone.”

The exact date she died is still unknown, but the toxicology tests will help determine if foul play was involved.

A spokesperson for Greek police said: “No other evidence has emerged from the body or the suitcase that would allow us to identify another person.

“We are awaiting the result of toxicology tests to determine the cause of death, and ascertain whether foul play was involved.

“The investigation is ongoing.”



First Minister John Swinney said Ross’s family would be supported by the Scottish government and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “This is an absolutely appalling case that has been reported overnight.

“And obviously I’m deeply concerned that such a tragedy has taken place.”

News.title: We can only hope Gianni Infantino’s naked greed ultimately leads to his downfall
News.content:
Bully for Uefa

SOMETIMES the school bully just needs someone to stand up and deliver them a much-needed thump.

Europe’s footballing governing bodies came together to deliver just such a blow to Gianni Infantino.



Fifa’s pound-shop mafioso president united the globe in outrage at his cash-grab plans to sell off the World Cup.

Infantino likely stood to make millions personally from his shameless deal.

By effectively bribing and blackmailing weaker federations for support, he hoped his plan would succeed. But yesterday, it was surely killed stone dead.



Uefa’s threat that ALL European teams would boycott the World Cup shredded Infantino’s grubby scheme.

It is inconceivable that a tournament without powerhouses Spain, France, England, Portugal, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany or Italy could survive.

What multinational companies would be thrilled by the prospect of paying tens of millions of dollars to sponsor a World Cup without any nation from a continent of 743million people?

In a powerful statement Uefa said: “There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. Some things are simply too important to sell.”

Quite right. Infantino and his acolytes made the mistake of thinking the World Cup was theirs to trade.

We can only hope his naked greed ultimately leads to his downfall.



Cut off the cash

DURING the weeks of choppy waters in the Channel, we were told that France was finally helping to smash the gangs.

Suddenly, the weather is clear, hundreds are arriving daily and the French cops have reverted to their traditional uselessness.

French emergency services swarmed on to a beach yesterday when four migrants were tragically found dead.

Wouldn’t it be better to commit similar effort and resources BEFORE such needless loss of life?

Britain has handed £1billion to France since 2018. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood warned in April when she signed the latest £662million deal that it depended on results.



She must now consider pausing the flow of cash to Paris.

Date with hate

THE Green mayor of Hackney Zoe Garbett was forced to apologise yesterday for demanding Haifa, Israel, respond to her plans to end twinning arrangements between the two places by . . . October 7.

She claims choosing the notorious date of the murder of 1,200 Jews by Hamas terrorists was accidental. Really?

The Green Party — taken over by poisonous, hate-filled fanatics — is showing its true colours in power.

News.title: Builder, 36, died just weeks after scooping £25k jackpot online prize draw – as tributes pour in
News.content:
'LOYAL & GENUINE' Builder, 36, died just weeks after scooping £25k jackpot online prize draw – as tributes pour in

A BUILDER has died just weeks after winning a £25,000 jackpot, prompting heartrending tributes to flood in.

Carl Blakemore, 36, was found dead after winning the prize money from an online competition site just weeks beforehand.



The provisional cause of death was given as hanging, an inquest heard.

Described as a “hardworking and genuine lad” by his colleagues, Carl from Tonyrefail, South Wales, was said to have made a “lasting impact on everyone”.



Carl’s bosses at Davies Contractors Ltd are now urging people to “speak to others” and “break the stigma around men’s mental health“.

The firm said: “Carl wasn’t just an employee – he was part of our family.



“He was a hardworking, loyal, genuine lad who made a lasting impact on everyone who had the privilege of working alongside him.

“His passing has deeply affected every single one of us at Davies.



“It is a reminder that life is precious and that behind every smile, there can be battles that others cannot see.”

They added that mental health can affect people from “all walks of life”, stressing the importance of checking up on friends, family and workmates.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

“A simple conversation can make all the difference,” they said.

“Rest easy, Carl. You will always be part of the Davies family.”

The construction company held a family fun day in a bid to raise funds for Carl’s grieving family.



The tragic news follows his successful entry in a prize draw run by the online company Vortex.

The site offers participants the chance to win Audi cars, campervans and even £50,000 in cash.

A spokesperson for Vortex shared a tribute to Carl, with the message: “This is Carl. He won £25,000 off us a few weeks ago.”

“Carl sadly passed away last week and I’ve been bombarded with messages telling me the news.”

They added that the company intended to raise money to assist Carl’s family with funeral costs.



A full inquest into his death is due to take place in Pontypridd, South Wales, at a date yet to be confirmed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

News.title: Chilling rise of Scandi child soldiers as kids as young as nine are recruited as assassins for ultra-violent cartels
News.content:
BABY-FACED Johannes Natland left his middle-class parents’ comfortable home on the Norwegian coast “to play football with friends” – then the aspiring lawyer disappeared.

A heavy drug user, Natland — who had just turned 18 — told his then-girlfriend: “It will be a bit cool to really kill someone.”





Days later, gun-toting cops ­hammered on the door of a Huddersfield hotel room 500 miles away in West Yorkshire.

In his underwear, Natland emerged and feebly cocked his hands at the armed British police officers to mimic a gun.

But this was no game. Pushing his face into the corridor wall, officers cuffed him and read him his rights.

Under the bed inside the room, they found a 9mm semi-automatic Luger pistol, a revolver, 12 rounds of live ammunition and £2,000 in cash.

On Wednesday an Old Bailey jury found Natland guilty of conspiring to murder an unknown target in the UK. He will be sentenced in October.

This bright and sporty youngster had been recruited online to be a teenage assassin by the Iranian-linked Foxtrot international crime syndicate.

His reward if successful? A blood money bounty of £21,000.

Natland’s mother, journalist Ellen Kongsnes said before her son’s trial that she found the turn of events “completely incomprehensible”.





She added: “It feels like a very bad movie, with a terribly bad script that doesn’t seem realistic at all.”

Yet Natland is one of hundreds of teens recruited across Scandinavia to maim and kill for ultra-violent criminal cartels like Foxtrot.

The Scandi child hoodlums have wreaked carnage in Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and now the UK.

Over a four-month period in 2024 at least 25 Swedish youngsters on suspected contract-killing or bombing missions were arrested in Denmark.

The ground zero for the rise of these child soldiers is Sweden. Long a standard bearer for liberal tolerance, the land of Ikea and ABBA seems from the outside an unlikely haven for teenage assassins.

Yet children as young as 11 have been caught with automatic weapons, while nine-year-old boys act as street-corner lookouts for mobsters.

In one court case it emerged a 15-year-old, who committed murder for around £6,300 in cash, had written to a friend: “I shot I kill.”

The pal’s sickening response was: “Hahahahahaha. Head shot?”



So what attracts Swedish youngsters to the gangster world?

On a visit to capital Stockholm I met 6ft 2in Essa Sallah Kah. Using the street name Big Daddy or The Boss, he once ruled the 150-strong Chosen Ones mob.

Born in violence-ravaged Gambia, West Africa, his family moved to the gang-plagued Rinkeby estate where Essa became mob footsoldier aged just 12.

Powerfully built, he was soon acting as muscle for the area’s Yugoslav and ­Turkish gangs.

He says: “They were drug dealers. They drove nice cars and people had respect for them.

“I wanted to prove that we blacks can do it too. The attitude was, ‘Don’t come and f*** around with us’.”

He began carrying guns — AK-47 assault rifles or Colt handguns — and robbing shops or acting as a menacing debt collector.

Big Daddy then established the Chosen Ones and ­wallowed in the trappings of gangster life.



Driving a Mercedes, he and his retinue of bodyguards secured the best seats in Stockholm’s clubs, adding: “Wherever I went, I had a table. I didn’t stand in queues.” Reaching his 40s, he was a cocaine and amphetamine-addled, 36st mental and physical wreck.

Turning his back on his gangster life and finding God, the 53-year-old — now a social worker — told me: “People saw me as this dangerous guy, but I was anxious inside.

“None of the people who are doing this are happy.”

Yet the cartels — flooding social media with the lure of cash, notoriety and the high life — ­continue to attract wayward youth.

The business model has been compared to the gig economy that employs Uber drivers and Amazon delivery workers.

The gangsters — mostly adults — target children through Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok.

The cash rewards can be irresistible for youngsters living in poverty.

Lobbing a grenade — often used as a crude warning to rival gangsters rather than to kill — is valued at around £4,000, while a murder can earn the perpetrator £12,000.



And it’s not just boys looking for street cred and social media likes — teenage girls in Sweden are touting themselves as hitwomen.

In May, a 12-year-old was convicted after she threw two live hand grenades at a door in Boras, near Gothenburg, last year.

Recruited on social media for cash, she travelled by bus with the devices concealed in her clothing to target relatives of a rival gangland figure.

The grenades failed to detonate. The girl faced no penalty or sentence because she is below 15 — Sweden’s age of criminal responsibility.

Sweden’s Justice minister Gunnar Strommer said: “Girls’ participation in criminal circles is much more widespread than we had previously assumed.”

Stockholm prosecutor Ida Arnell said last year: “I had a case involving a 15-year-old girl recruited to shoot someone in the head.

“She was able to choose the type of mission — to aim at the guy’s door or his head. She chose the head.”

The girl was arrested with a 17-year-old male accomplice, who ended up pulling the trigger. The ­victim was left clinging to life after a shower of bullets lodged in their neck, stomach and legs.



The prosecutor added that girls “have to show that they are even more determined and tougher (than boys) to get the job.” Some 280 ­Swedish girls aged between 15 and 17 were charged with murder, ­manslaughter or other violent crimes in 2024. It is unclear how many were linked to organised crime.

In March, a 15-year-old girl was held in connection with the murder of two teenage boys, one from the southern city of Malmo and the other from the outskirts of Stockholm.

Astonishingly, a new trend shows children not yet in their teens are being recruited by Swedish gangs to conduct violent crime.

Ten children aged seven to 12 were arrested last year on suspicion of ­carrying out violent crimes for gangs.

Many youngsters come from ­Sweden’s immigrant communities. Famed for welcoming asylum seekers from the world’s trouble spots, ­politicians from all parties ­say Sweden has not managed to successfully integrate migrants.

Author and investigative reporter Diamant Salihu, 42, told me: “There’s a consensus now that Sweden has failed with integration.

“Germany has taken in a lot of migrants, but you don’t hear about child soldiers there.”

Much of the rise in Sweden’s teen gangsters traces back to the blood-thirsty cartel Foxtrot, which has links to the Iranian regime.

Its godfather, Rawa Majid, was born in Iran to Kurdish Iraqi parents before the family moved to Sweden.

Known as the Kurdish Fox, his young footsoldiers specialised in ­contract killings and bombing rivals. In 2023 Majid began a feud with one-time friend Ismail Abdo — nicknamed The Strawberry — who had become leader of rival gang Rumba.



Abdo’s mother was murdered at her home in Uppsala, north of Stockholm, by a 15 and 19-year-old. The violence soon spiralled.

In 2024 a string of attacks against Jewish or Israeli targets occurred.

There was a shooting outside the Israeli embassy in Stockholm. Then two Swedish teenagers aged 16 and 19 were arrested in Denmark after hand grenades were detonated near the Israeli embassy in Copenhagen.

Mossad, the Israeli intelligence agency, alleged Majid was working with Iran and blamed both Foxtrot and Rumba for the attacks.

It was Foxtrot that later enticed Norwegian Natland. Recruited by a teen known by the internet alias UnknownHustler, the lad from ­Stavanger was sent a blunt tender for a prospective assassination.

On 15 March 2025, UnknownHustler forwarded him a message reading: “Killing in England 270k (270,000 Norwegian Kroner is about £21,000).

“Have transport ready out of the country. Will smuggle assassin out of the country.

“The police will be paid to look the other way. Nothing can go wrong.”

Natland was then added to a chat group that included a Stavanger-based recruiter named Generalen and another nicknamed Agent 47.

Agent 47 was Ali Shehab, a 22-year-old Swedish-Iraqi gangster and a senior recruiter for Foxtrot.



Natland’s first message to the group — named Assassin EU — was, “Who is to be killed?”

It’s unclear if he was ever told the answer. Just two days later, Natland flew on a one-way ticket from Stavanger to Manchester.

Taking a taxi to Huddersfield, his handlers directed him to where cash and firearms were concealed under rubbish and in woodland.

Paying cash for a room in the Briar Court Hotel, he sent friends videos of himself with the guns.

As the minutes ticked by before the hit, recruiter Generalen was arrested at Oslo airport. Cops found messages about a planned “assassination” in England on his phone.

At 5:15am on March 19 last year cops raided Room 207 at the Briar Court Hotel. Marching out, the green dots from the officers’ guns shone on Natland’s chest.

Foxtrot’s teenage hitman had been stopped. Yet there are seemingly many more ready to take his place.

News.title: Andy Burnham hints at North Sea oil U-turn as he tells Trump he won’t ignore energy reserves
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has told Donald Trump he would not ignore the oil and gas in the North Sea while people are struggling with energy bills.

The Prime Minister said that he had reassured the US President he would take a “pragmatic approach” to drilling.



Mr Trump has long been lobbying for Britain to ramp up North Sea exploration and has railed against wind turbines.

Labour made an election commitment to ban any new drilling licences from being issued as part of Ed Miliband’s Net Zero drive.



But it is thought Mr Burnham, who moved Mr Miliband to the Foreign Office, could be more willing to exploit the energy in the North Sea.

On a visit to Cumbria on Thursday, the PM said: “I indicated in the phone call that we had a week last Monday that I would take a pragmatic approach when it comes to the North Sea, and that is my intention as we go forward from here.

“There is a resource there. When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that.”

There had been confusion on Mr Burnham’s first day in office earlier this month when Mr Trump said he would be “opening up, all the way” North Sea oil reserves.

But deputy Labour leader Lucy Powell said the manifesto commitment to ban new licences would stay in place.

A possible compromise could be to give the go-ahead to the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields that are awaiting decisions.



Both have already been granted licences but need approval from new Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has demanded Mr Burnham make the decisions without delay and expand drilling in the North Sea.

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said doing it “would be the first step towards ending Labour’s Net Zero madness that is driving up costs for families and businesses and holding our economy back”.

News.title: Greek cops rush to find CCTV after pinpointing when Brit’s body found in suitcase was placed in abandoned building
News.content:
GREEK cops are rushing to find CCTV of the abandoned building where a Brit woman was found stuffed in a suitcase as they close in on a timeline.

Elisabeth Ross, 38, was last seen leaving a friend’s house in Athens before her dead body was found 72 hours later.



The homeless man who made the grim discovery on July 18 has insisted that the suitcase was not in the building the two days prior.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building at 7 Evelpidon Street on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.



They are now combing the area for security cameras that might have captured the suitcase dump.

Local hotels and residences are also being examined, with police speculating that the body was likely taken to the building from close quarters.

Elisabeth arrived in Athens on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

She is said to have stayed at a friend’s house in Attica before leaving on July 15 with plans to meet American pals in Kypseli.



But her body was found at the abandoned building three days later, with no visible wounds on the body or any clear signs of a struggle.

Police quickly opened a murder investigation fearing a killer may be on the loose.

Cops are desperate to uncover what happened to Elisabeth during the three days she is unaccounted for – with the homeless man’s testimony giving them a strong lead.



Police spokesperson Konstantia Dimoglidou told The Sun: “The key to this case is to find out what happened to the woman during those three days as we don’t know anything about her moves on the 15th, 16th and 17th.

“The main focus is to find her cause of death as the medical examiner did not find any signs of struggle or injury on her body.

“We are waiting for the toxicology reports to shed some light in the next few days.

“We cannot be talking about a murder if we don’t know what happened to her – maybe she died and someone tried to hide her body, anything is possible and at this point it’s too soon to tell.

“As part of the investigation we are also checking CCTV from the area where she was found and we are working to trace her phone.”



The exact date she died is still unknown, but the toxicology tests will help determine if foul play was involved.

A spokesperson for Greek police said: “No other evidence has emerged from the body or the suitcase that would allow us to identify another person.

“We are awaiting the result of toxicology tests to determine the cause of death, and ascertain whether foul play was involved.

“The investigation is ongoing.”

Cops are also reportedly still probing a theory that Elisabeth may have been lured to the abandoned location by a homeless person.



Officials are also still trying to pin down the route Elisabeth took to get into Kypseli and are quizzing local hotels and bars to see if they recognise her.

The friends who hosted the Scottish woman during her holiday have also been questioned and confirmed she left under her own power and appeared to be in good spirits.

It comes as her heartbroken dad revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her mysterious death.

The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek cops he was sent several messages for two weeks after Elisabeth’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.

An officer told the Sun that the emergence of the messages has helped investigators track the location of phone.



They said: “They were sent from Athens and it is clear whoever sent them was trying to buy time.”

Elisabeth’s phone was only turned off on Wednesday morning after reports of the body being found made global headlines, local media claim.

First Minister John Swinney said Ross’s family would be supported by the Scottish government and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “This is an absolutely appalling case that has been reported overnight.

“And obviously I’m deeply concerned that such a tragedy has taken place.”

News.title: Dating app rapist jailed after victims expose sickening pattern of abuse
News.content:
Dating app rapist jailed after victims expose sickening pattern of abuse

Muhammad Ans, 29, has been jailed for 20 years and placed on the sex offenders register for life after being convicted of raping three women he met on dating apps

View 2 Images Muhammad Ans has been jailed for his crimes (Image: Devon and Cornwall Police )

A serial rapist who attacked multiple women he met on dating apps has been jailed for 20 years.

‌



Muhammad Ans was convicted of four counts of rape against three women following a two-week trial at Plymouth Crown Court.

‌



The 29-year-old will also serve a further three years on extended licence and has been placed on the sex offenders register for life.

‌



Ans met his victims on various dating apps - Tinder, Bumble and Baddoo - between 2023 and 2025, the court heard.

One woman told police how after she was raped by Ans, he offered to pay her $3,000 in compensation if she would "leave it".

He began contacting the first woman on Bumble before arranging to meet in person near the end of 2023.

‌



The pair met and went out for a meal before Ans took the woman back to his accommodation in Coventry and raped her. He then went on to rape her again in a series of events in early 2024.

He messaged the victim again in August 2024 asking to meet up.

She confronted him about raping her over a number of messages, and he "apologised and offered to take her out shopping and to go for meals together". The woman refused.

‌



Days later, Ans met his second victim on the Baddoo app. By this time, he had moved to Tavistock and was living in a flat.

View 2 Images The sentencing was heard at Plymouth Crown Court (file) (Image: Carl Eve/PlymouthLive)

He messaged his second victim before meeting up with her in his car and taking her back to his flat, where they drank alcohol.

‌



The victim made it clear that she did not want to have sex, but Ans raped her.

Messages shown in court between Ans and his second victim show that after he dropped her home, she messaged him and challenged him about the rape.

Ans responded to his second victim by apologising, adding "that he couldn't stop himself".

‌



He offered to take his second victim shopping and claimed he wanted to get to know her and go to the beach with her. The victim refused and told him she was going to report him for raping her.

The same day, the victim reported Ans, and Detective Constable Craig Ferguson was appointed as the case officer, reports Plymouth Live.

Ans was identified, and his vehicle details were established by the police. A wanted appeal was issued for Ans, and he was located in Leeds after fleeing Tavistock.

‌



During an interview, Ans denied the offence, but admitted that he had met the victim. He claimed all sexual contact had been consensual and that his admissions in the messages were "confusion on his part despite his clear acknowledgement and apologies."

His phone was seized by police and taken for examination. Ans was bailed on conditions not to contact the victim.

In August 2025, another victim was identified by police. She told police she met Ans through Tinder and had gone for a drink with him before they went back to her address, where he raped her.

‌



Ans was further arrested in relation to the third victim and was charged and remanded.

During the examination of Ans' phone, DC Ferguson found messages between Ans and his first victim, who was then identified and confirmed that she had also been raped by Ans.

He was then charged with these offences as well, and the cases of all three victims were joined.

‌



During sentencing, the court heard from all three women raped by Ans.

The first victim said: "I'm finding it hard to describe the initial impact of Ans' rape. After the violent event occurred, it felt like I had to burn everything that made up the woman I was, so that then it would have happened to her rather than me.

"I rarely slept, and when I did, nightmares accompanied me. My anxiety was through the roof, supplemented by intrusive thoughts, intense nausea, and debilitating panic attacks.

‌



"Ans clearly saw the pain he had inflicted on me and then went on to hurt others in the same way. I truly believe that he is a dangerous and predatory man. No sentence can undo the damage he has caused or the years I will continue to live with the consequences of his actions."

In a statement, the second victim said: "When I think about what Ans did to me; him raping me started a chain of events that have led to some of the darkest and most difficult times that I have faced in my life.

"I still feel an intense amount of anger and rage towards him. I had told him 'NO', and I had pushed his hands away and pulled my leggings back up. My words meant nothing to him, and I now recognise that he had already decided what was going to happen to me, regardless of whether I consented to it or not.

‌



"People think that a rapist is someone hiding down an alley, or in a bush with a knife, that will drag you away and force themselves on you... but Ans made me realise that a rapist can be charismatic, educated and can arrive with a smile.

"Regardless of how he portrayed himself to me and others he is nothing but a rapist monster. He is a disgusting human being, and I hate him with every part of me."

The third victim said: "In terms of the physical impact, it took me many weeks before I was able to sleep properly again. Even now, I continue to experience nightmares and flashbacks relating to what happened. I became scared to be at home on my own in-case he showed up, my own home felt wrong and unsafe.

‌



"Psychologically, the impact of these events has affected almost every aspect of my life. I have suffered from severe anxiety and panic attacks as a result of my experience with Ans.

"The events have significantly affected my ability to trust others, particularly men. I find it difficult to form new relationships now as a result. As a girl who just wanted her happy ending, I feel I have paid a high price for trying to find it.

"I see Ans as directly responsible for my current symptoms and state of mind. If I hadn't met him and he hadn't done these things to me, I believe that I would be in a very different position now in my life. I feel that he is a risk to women, and that he used me sexually despite me making my boundaries clear."

‌



Sentencing, Judge Matthew Turner KC said each victim was in "a vulnerable position" in their lives at the time of Ans' horrific crimes. He added that the woman initially found Ans charming, but he preyed upon that to rape them and satisfy his own sexual desires.

Judge Turner said that Ans's lack of recognition of his criminality was "deeply troubling", adding that there was a complete disconnect between how he viewed his actions and the "single-minded pursuit of your own sexual gratification". Ans will also be required to sign the sex offenders register for life.

DC Ferguson said evidence in the case "clearly showed" that Ans had "made the same types of comments and offers towards each victim after raping them."

‌



He added: "This included apologising to them, telling them that it was a mistake, and that people make mistakes when first meeting, as well as offers of giving certain victims money and to take them shopping.

"In relation to one of the victims, it was also explained that he had offered to pay her $3,000 in compensation if she would 'leave it'. This victim refused his offer and had screenshot the messages he had sent, and sent these on as part of her evidence.

"Ans is a sexual predator who targeted these women on dating sites with the sole purpose of meeting up with them for sex. His motivation was clear. These women were looking for meaningful relationships, and were not seeking casual sexual encounters, and they made this clear to Ans.

Article continues below

"Despite this Ans created situations where they were each caused to be alone with him, and he then proceeded to rape them, and forced them into depraved sexual acts. Ans was driven by his sexual appetite, and the voices of his victims did not matter to him. He chose what was going to happen, and he forced his will onto others.

"Their clear boundaries and lack of consent did not matter to him."

DC Ferguson said the victims displayed "tremendous courage and strength" by giving evidence and that Devon and Cornwall Police would remain committed to "supporting women and girls who are victims of violence, and those persons who have been the victim of sexual offences."

News.title: Crete wildfires live: Rethymno in flames amid mass evacuations on Greek islands
News.content:
Flames are tearing across Greek Islands, forcing the evacuation of entire villages on Crete, Paros and Andros as wildfires continue to sweep across Europe

Raging wildfires have taken hold across several Greek islands, forcing villages to be evacuated as firefighters struggle to contain the flames.

Wildfires in the Rethymno region of the south of Crete are burning "out of control on all fronts", with firefighting aircraft unable to be deployed due to strong winds. Thousands of people, including tourists, were evacuated overnight. Urgent evacuation orders have also been issued for parts of Paros and Andros.

Three firefighters have died in Greece, with two becoming trapped in a vehicle while tackling the flames in Rethymno. Meanwhile, Europe's emergency response chief warned that the entire continent could be engulfed as wildfires rage in France, Spain and Portugal.

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if [it is] there as well, we will have all Europe on fire," Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said yesterday.

News.title: Boy, 1, boiled alive in blistering hot bath after mum and boyfriend abandoned him
News.content:
Boy, 1, boiled alive in blistering hot bath after mum and boyfriend abandoned him

WARNING DISTRESSING CONTENT: Samantha Garver, 26, and her boyfriend Sergio Mena, 34, have been jailed forllowing the horriffic death of Garver's 1-year-old son Henry Wheatley-Brown in California

View 4 Images Henry Wheatley-Brown, 1, died in agony (Image: ABC7)

A California couple have been sentenced to more than a decade behind bars for the brutal murder of a 1-year-old.

‌



Samantha Garver, 26, and her boyfriend Sergio Mena, 34, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and child abuse causing great bodily injury to her 1-year-old son, Henry Wheatley-Brown.

‌



Little Henry died in horrific circumstances while in Mena’s care at the couple's home near in Sugarloaf, near Big Bear City, California on September 30, 2023.

‌



Wheatley-Brown died from severe burns after Mena put the toddler in a "scalding" hot bath and abandoned him, allegedly to pick up methamphetamine.

Following an investigation authorities said the boy was the victim of ongoing abuse after suffering second- and third-degree burns on his body as well as bodily bruising and several healing fractures in both arms.

View 4 Images The 1-year-old suffered terrible injuries (Image: ABC7)

‌



Child services also concluded following an investigation that the cause of the toddler's death was "abuse or neglect,” The Daily Express US reports.

Upon returning to the house Mena found the little boy screaming in agony after getting "severely burned" in the bath, according to the San Bernardino County District Attorney's Office. However, he made no effort to help relieve the boy's pain, prosecutors allege.

"Despite Henry's extensive and life-threatening injuries, neither defendant sought medical care, instead attempting to treat the burns with over‑the‑counter ointment," prosecutors said.

‌



It wasn't until the following day that the couple alerted authorities to his "shallow breathing." The district attorney's office said, "Paramedics found Henry without a pulse, ice‑cold to the touch and severely dehydrated."

View 4 Images Sergio Mena, 34, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and child abuse causing great bodily injury while Samantha Garver, 36, was convicted of manslaughter and child abuse causing great bodily injury (Image: ABC7)

The district attorney's office said in a statement, "Although nothing can bring back baby Henry or erase the suffering he endured, today's sentences deliver justice and ensure these defendants will never again harm a child. The San Bernardino County District Attorney's Office will honour Henry's memory by never forgetting him and by continuing to fight for vulnerable children."

‌



Sergio Mena, will spend 21 years behind bars while Samantha Garver will spend 14 years in jail.

There are years' worth of records documenting the alleged abuse that the little boy and his three older siblings suffered, which led to the San Bernardino County Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS) getting involved with Garber, according to The Los Angeles Times.

View 4 Images Samantha Garver will spend 14 years behind bars (Image: ABC7)

‌



The mother allegedly told staff at DCFS that she "felt like putting a pillow over" one of her children to stop their relentless crying, and posted a question on Facebook inquiring whether "duct taping a child's mouth is abusive."

The perplexing case led investigators to have differing views on the situation, with some saying the children faced "high risk" of abuse while another argued the children were "safe."

The child's own family members seemed to dismiss the severity of the child abuse occurring at home. The boy's grandmother, Sierra Rivers, appeared to argue that abuse is commonplace, acceptable, and can be overcome.

Article continues below

"I got abused as a kid, and I got hit as a baby, and I turned out fine," Rivers told The Los Angeles Times.

News.title: Ten mountain climbers missing after massive avalanche atop world-famous peak
News.content:
Ten mountain climbers missing after massive avalanche atop world-famous peak

Around 10 climbers, including record-breaking mountaineer Nirmal Purja, are feared missing after an avalanche hit Broad Peak in Concordia, northern Pakistan

Ten climbers are feared missing after an avalanche hit Pakistan's Broad Peak - the 12th highest mountain in the world.

The group, led by Nepali mountaineer and former British Marine Nirmal Purja, have been out of contact for several hours since the avalanche hit on Thursday afternoon, the Alpine Club of Pakistan said.

News.title: Suffolk fire live: Hundreds of firefighters battle 'unprecedented' wildfire near nuclear plant
News.content:
A wildfire is raging in Dunwich Heath, Suffolk where evacuations have been ordered - the blaze is close to three nuclear plant sites, and has burned an area the size of 210 football pitches

Hundreds of firefighters are battling through the night to contain a massive wildfire in Dunwich Heath, Suffolk, that has devasted a huge nature reserve and threatened a nearby nuclear power plant.

Temperatures soared into the mid-30s in southern England on Thursday, burning an area the size of 210 football pitches in a National Trust reserve just a few miles away from Sizewell B - the UK's largest nuclear power plant.

Some 200 caravans were evacuated this morning, with holidaymakers woken up by banging on their doors. Eighteen fire engines and more than 100 firefighters are now at the scene, with authorities saying they expect crews to be battling the blaze for the next two days.

There is also concern for wildlife in the area, after nature reserve RSPB Minsmere announcing its closure this morning. RSPB Suffolk area manager Adam Rowlands said the land was home to rare wildlife including nightjars - and it could take "more than a decade" for the habitat to recover.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the fire service will have “all of the support” they need in tackling the blaze.

On Thursday afternoon, an EDF spokesperson said the fire was “not affecting operations at Sizewell B power station”.

News.title: 'A broken system has held back towns and cities for too long - it doesn’t have to be like this'
News.content:
'A broken system has held back towns and cities for too long - it doesn’t have to be like this'

Andy Burnham's close ally and First Secretary of State, Louise Haigh, writes for The Mirror as the PM unveils plans to give mayors a slice of their area's income tax

View Image First Secretary of State Louise Haigh with Andy Burnham at No10 North (Image: James Speakman/The Times/PA Wire)

The days of Westminster hoarding power are over. When Andy Burnham stood on the steps of Downing Street last week, he promised that this Government would put communities back in the driving seat - and that’s exactly what we’re going to do.

‌



For forty years, more and more decisions about the future of our towns and cities have been taken behind closed doors in Whitehall. People living hundreds of miles away choosing where and how money is spent, but with no real understanding of the challenges facing the people who live there.

‌



It’s a broken system that has held back too many places for far too long. It’s drained power and investment away from our communities, hollowed out our high streets and left our young people struggling to find decent jobs.

‌



But it doesn’t have to be like this.

When the Prime Minister launched No.10 North in Manchester last week he promised to rewire the country, drive good growth in every postcode and put local people back in control of their own futures. Today, we’re kickstarting that change with the biggest transfer of power and resource in a generation.

‌



EMBARGOED 2230 Andy Burnham unveils plan to give mayors slice of income tax from area READ MORE :

No two towns or cities are the same, so every local leader should have the flexibility they need to help their communities flourish. From employment to housing, transport to infrastructure - we are reshaping how decisions are made so that places have the powers they need to improve public services, encourage local investment and deliver real benefits for the people living there.

Instead of Westminster calling the shots, local leaders will have far more control over how money raised locally is spent. This gives each area the opportunity to channel investment into the areas that matter most to them. Whether improving local bus services or building new council homes - communities will have more powers to decide their priorities and more control over how they spend their money.

The changes we’re announcing today will also give mayors and local councils new powers to combine education, employment and health support, making it easier to help young people into work. By partnering with local businesses and employers, we can make sure they have the skills and training they need to take up the jobs and apprenticeships available in their local area.

Article continues below

This is what it means to rewire Britain and put people back in control. Over the coming weeks and months, we’ll be working closely with Mayors and council leaders to make sure they have the powers to solve local problems and seize local opportunities.

This is how we start putting people back in the driving seat, create new jobs and apprenticeships for our young people and get our high streets thriving again. It’s how we drive good growth in every postcode and get the country back on the right path.

News.title: Mayors to keep slice of income tax and business rates for local projects in devolution revolution
News.content:
Mayors to keep slice of income tax and business rates for local projects in devolution revolution

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the huge devolution shake-up will allow local leaders to keep more of the cash residents pay - and invest in their communities

View 2 Images Andy Burnham and his Chancellor John Healey at No10 North last week (Image: Christopher Furlong/PA Wire)

Andy Burnham is set to unveil plans to give mayors in England a share of income tax and business rates for the first time as part of a huge devolution shake-up.

The new Prime Minister and former Greater Manchester Mayor said it will allow local leaders to keep a slice of the cash collected from their residents to invest in their communities.

It is being billed as the biggest transfer of power and funding from Westminster in a generation.

The government said the rate of income tax which billpayers face will not change as a direct result of the reforms. But details - including the level of income tax retention for local leaders - will be set out in the new Chancellor John Healey’s first Budget in the autumn.

Ahead of an announcement on Friday, Mr Burnham said: “I said we'd take power out of Westminster and carry it into every postcode in the country. Today, we make good on that promise. Under our plans, more of the taxes raised in a community will stay in that community.”

Voting opens in biggest ever by-election to replace Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor READ MORE :

View 2 Images 'For the first time we’re giving mayors a share of income tax so communities directly benefit,' says Chancellor John Healey (Image: Simon Dawson / No 10 Downing Street)

He added: “Soon, every local leader will have the power and resources to improve public transport, build homes and create jobs. I know what it's like to be ignored by politicians in Westminster. I'm not going to make that same mistake now I'm PM.

"The whole of government will now pull together behind the people and places that desperately need our support. This is how we'll bring back hope and bring power home to you.”

Mr Healey said: “The people who best understand what skills employers want, what transport an area needs and where investment can make the biggest difference are those who live there.

“For the first time we’re giving mayors a share of income tax so communities directly benefit when their economy grows - passing power out of Westminster and driving growth in every postcode.”

Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves also announced in her Mais lecture earlier this year that the Treasury was looking at giving regional mayors “control of a share of some national taxes which have, for too long, been allocated by central government”

Working with the new No10 North, the government also said local leaders will also gain more control over services including housing, transport, and skills.

This will include powers to bring rail and bus services under greater local control and get local trams and metros built faster.

Angela Rayner, the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government, added: “Our devolution revolution is about bringing an end to the begging-bowl culture of the past, and instead making sure our local leaders have the tools they need to drive the change that communities have been crying out for.”

News.title: Tourists among thousands of people evacuated on Crete as wildfires kills two firefighters
News.content:
Tourists among thousands of people evacuated on Crete as wildfires kills two firefighters

Two firefighters have died on Crete after becoming trapped while tackling a wildfire, several of which are raging through the mountains on Greece's largest island

BREAKING France forest fires- Thousands of tourists evacuated from campsites popular with Brits

Thousands of people - including tourists - were evacuated on the island of Crete today as wildfires claimed the lives of three firefighters in Greece. Two died on the island after becoming trapped while tackling a fire near Krya Vrysi in the Rethymno region. A third firefighter died on the Greek mainland, near the port town of Gytheio in the Peloponnese.

‌



As gusts reached 125km/h (77mph) on the island, around 8,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight but were later allowed to return. Amid France's fires, George and Amal Clooney were forced to evacuate their home.

‌



The actor admitted he had "no idea" whether the home he shares with human rights lawyer Amal in Brignoles, a village in the south, will make it through "this terrible moment".

‌



View 5 Images A firefighter tackles a blaze on Crete (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

New Outlander-themed tourism guide highlights pair of Stirling attractions READ MORE :

Huge 7ft 4in man dies aged 33 after complications with growing too tall READ MORE :

In a letter addressed to Didier Bremond, mayor of Brignoles, Clooney promised the pair are "committed" to supporting the community in the aftermath of the natural disaster.

The letter, which was shared by Clooney's publicist Guido Gotz, read: "Dear Didier, At this point we have no idea whether our beautiful home makes it through this terrible moment.

‌



View 5 Images Smoke rises from wildfires on the island of Crete (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The letter read: "As we evacuate Brignoles we want to emphasise two things, first we hope you and the people of our city are safe.

"Second that Amal and I are committed to making sure that whatever happens to our village, we are part of this community and we'll be part of making it whole. We love Brignoles and our friends who live there."

‌



The pair moved to France permanently in 2021 after purchasing an estate which Clooney described as their "farm in France".

The couple and their twins, Ella and Alexander, were awarded their French citizenship in December.

Greece, France, Spain and Turkey are among many European countries facing devastating fires and drought.

‌



View 5 Images Amal and George Clooney in France

Several fires have continued to burn in Spain and Portugal, although Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared an end to the national emergency for wildfires in the Ávila and Madrid regions. In south-west France, some residents have been able to return to their homes after a major wildfire in the Gironde region. The fire raging on Crete broke out in the Rethymno region and has spread rapidly, destroying homes and agricultural land. It remains one of the biggest fires currently active on the island and is still burning out of control. There was no clear picture of the destruction so far, Rethymno's deputy regional governor Maria Lioni said, adding that containing the fire was the main priority. Lioni described the "dark day" for the region as gusts overnight reached up to 11 on the Beaufort scale - a wind force categorised as "violent" - fanning the flames and hampering containment efforts.

View 5 Images Wildfires have raged across southwestern France (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Some of those evacuated in Rethymno were moved into a temporary shelter. "It was frightening," British tourist Peter Wood said.

"We could see the flames in the hills above the village, and the police and firefighters were just telling everyone to leave straight away." The blaze came during one of Crete's busiest months for tourism.

Hundreds of firefighters have been deployed to the region to battle the blaze.

‌



View 5 Images A firefighter's vehicle left damaged by the wildfires on Crete (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Hellenic Fire Service chief Theodoros Vagias expressed his condolences for the two firefighters who sacrificed their lives, naming them as 58-year-old Emmanouil Stratidakis and Pantelis Diamantakis, 25. Both will be buried today, the statement added. In the Madrid region, 24,000 people have been told they can return and restrictions on another 20,000 have been lifted.

Fourteen people died in the Almería region of Spain earlier this month, including UK and Belgian nationals as well as US, French and Spanish citizens.

Article continues below

Fires are also burning in neighbouring Portugal, in the north-eastern district of Vila Real.

News.title: Suffolk wildfire still growing and unpredictable, says fire service
News.content:
Homes and a holiday caravan park were evacuated after the fire broke out and there are fears for rare birds and wildlife whose home is the heath and nearby RSPB Minsmere.

The "large-scale, wind-driven" fire was declared a major incident on Thursday morning, due to the size and complexity of the blaze which was helped by south-westerly winds.

On Thursday evening, Suffolk's chief fire officer, Jon Lacey, said: "Eighteen fire engines and 120 firefighters are involved in the response, but difficult terrain and limited access routes are making it hard for crews to reach some areas of the wildfire."

An update on the fire service's website said it was being supported by firefighters from neighbouring brigades, with engines also being sent from London.

"We expect the response to continue for at least the next 48 hours."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to give the fire service "all the support it needs" to tackle the "very serious" heathland blaze.

Communities Secretary Angela Rayner praised firefighters for their "skill and dedication and bravery".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has called for Burnham to host an emergency Cobra meeting to discuss the outbreak of wildfires in Britain, including in Suffolk.
