A TSA agent discovered a set of stolen Civil War-era cannonballs in a passenger's suitcase during a routine security screening at an Alabama airport earlier this month, law enforcement officials said.

The Transportation Security Administration said in a statement Friday that the relics were discovered at Gulf Shores International Airport on July 18 after the agent observed what appeared to be a large, opaque item inside a suitcase during an X-ray screening. When he opened the luggage, he found five small cannonballs wrapped in paper towels and notified a supervisor.

“I had never seen anything quite this unique,” TSA Officer Justin Dupree said in a statement from the agency. “I’ve seen inert grenades and training munitions but never an Indiana Jones-esque stolen artifact-type situation.”

The cannonballs — the largest about the size of grapefruits and weighing about as much as a shot put ball — were inactive and didn’t contain any explosive material or active components, the TSA said. Still, cannonballs are artillery munitions and considered prohibited items on planes.

Police eventually determined the cannonballs were stolen from Fort Morgan, based on paint marking applied to the artifacts by fort staff, and that they dated to the American Civil War. The historic Gulf Shores fort played a significant role in several military conflicts, including the Civil War.

The Baldwin County Sheriff’s Office said Thursday that a juvenile stole the cannonballs from a storage area in the fort and then placed them in their grandmother’s checked bag. The grandmother told officers she did not know they were stolen.

Spokespersons for Fort Morgan didn't respond to a email seeking comment. The sheriff's office said the institution declined to press charges, and the artifacts were returned to the fort.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s selling football’s soul with World Cup plan – shifty Fifa chief needs stopping before it gets worse
Sports.content:
“WE will restore the image and respect of Fifa, and everyone in the world will applaud us.”

So said Gianni Infantino when he replaced the disgraced Sepp Blatter as president a little over ten years ago.



How’s that working out?

At the time, his colleagues considered him a good egg, a safe pair of hands to guide Fifa back towards the light after the corruption scandals of the previous regime.



Now, it’s quite clear he is more dangerous than bungling Blatter ever was.

He spent months sucking up to Donald Trump and, lo and behold, a plan emerged to sell off a huge stake in the World Cup, with the lead investor being a member of… the Trump family.



Now Fifa’s 211 members have until September 19 to vote through his scheme, and if they go along with it they’ll receive £15million straight off the bat.

The message is clear: “Make us rich and we’ll make you rich.”

Miguel Maduro, the former chair of Fifa’s governance committee, even went so far as to describe it as a “legalised bribe”.

Just when you think it’s impossible to have a greater contempt for Infantino, after six weeks of him gurning ridiculously on our TV screens, he sinks even lower.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The shameless Fifa chief, who went on a weird social media rant earlier this week slamming his haters, might be dressing it up as a plan to help smaller footballing nations.

But when the shifty Swiss is the one pulling the levers, it’s impossible not to suspect there is another agenda at play.

After all, he’s just spent six weeks rubbing shoulders with billionaire business leaders and sports commissioners in the US who earn ten or 20 times as much as he does.

When his embarrassing brown-nosing campaign with Trump began, it was sickening but on the whole it appeared harmless enough.



Anyone of sound body and mind will have seen the inaugural ‘Peace Prize’, gifted to Trump at the World Cup draw ceremony, for what it was.

He has been worming his way into the US President’s inner circle and as the two men have become chummier and chummier, the murkier their relationship has become.

It looked like we’d reached rock bottom during the World Cup, when Trump picked up the phone to his old mucker and asked him to rescind Folarin Balogun’s red card.

Infantino insists Trump’s intervention had nothing to do with the decision to suspend the suspension, trampling all over the integrity of the game in the process, but no one is buying it.

As enjoyable as large parts of the World Cup were, there was a ­suffocating, corporate Americanisation to the whole tournament that began to wear thin.



But if Infantino’s plan is waved through, it will only get worse.

He might claim that Fifa will retain all management of the World Cup but the billionaire investors will undoubtedly have an influence on how things are run.

They’re not doing it for the good of the game, they’re doing it to make money — and once Infantino opens the door to external investment, it’s the first step on a slippery slope.

It will mean hydration breaks become the norm at Fifa tournaments, so the football essentially turns into a game of four quarters, to create lucrative additional ad breaks.

The already bloated World Cup will be expanded to 64 teams, no matter how much of a knock-on effect it has on the quality of football or the welfare of players. Again to grow revenue.



You wouldn’t put it past them trying to make the tournament an annual event — and the Club World Cup will no doubt be up for expansion, too.

Fifa and Infantino have gradually chipped away at the soul of the greatest sporting event on the planet, and this sell-out will destroy it for good.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The associations with the power to do something about it need to show some backbone and stop him in his tracks.

Uefa’s 55 members threatening to boycott the World Cup, after their crisis meeting, is a good start.

Sports.title: Man Utd star cuts holiday short to return to training as he tries to put World Cup nightmare behind him
Sports.content:
SENNE LAMMENS cut his holiday short to dive back into Manchester United training and banish his World Cup nightmare.

The Belgian stopper, 24, was granted an extended break by Michael Carrick after his tournament heartbreak.



But rather than waiting until Monday, Lammens pitched up at Carrington on Thursday —keen to put his national team clanger behind him.

Lammens endured the most difficult moment of his young career in Belgium’s 2-1 quarter-final defeat to eventual winners Spain.



Coming on late for Thibaut Courtois proved disastrous, as Lammens spilled a shot that gifted Arsenal’s Mikel Merino an 88th-minute winner.

But United’s No1 refused to waste another day on the beach — with ESPN first revealing his drive to jump straight back into action.

Now, Old Trafford chiefs fully back the Belgian to be razor-sharp for the August 22 opener at Hull City, eager to protect a keeper who delivered a near-flawless debut season.

Lammens won the Prem’s best transfer award in May and helped United return to the Champions League following his £18.2m move from Belgian side Royal Antwerp.

Summer signing and Belgium captain Youri Tielemans also checked into first-team training on Thursday.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



Tielemans’ report date was pre-agreed when United triggered his £35m move from Aston Villa after his World Cup exit.

United are next in action against Atletico Madrid in Sweden on Saturday.

They then face pre-season matches against Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds United and Milan.

Lammens is unlikely to feature against Atletico, with Tom Heaton, Radek Vitek and Dermot Mee all receiving minutes between the sticks in United’s opening friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Sports.title: Infantino’s ludicrous World Cup plan dead in the water as 41 more countries reject plot after Uefa and England boycott
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO’S plan to sell the World Cup looks dead in the water after Concacaf joined Uefa in rejecting it – while his reign as Fifa head could soon be over too.

European powerbrokers are trying to convince Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi to challenge him at next year’s election in March.



Infantino, 56, has run unopposed at both of the previous two votes and is looking to secure a fourth term in office.

But he is facing mounting opposition after Uefa and Concacaf hit back at his outlandish scheme to flog stakes in the World Cup.



Concacaf nations convened a meeting with all presidents of its 41 member associations along with the North American, Central American and Caribbean body’s relevant chiefs and expressed their strong disagreements with Infantino’s plans.

A lengthy statement read: “Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first.

“Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organisation founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

“History has shown Fifa and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values.

“With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its Fifa Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the Fifa President to establish ‘Fifa Forward Enterprise’ and sell interests in the Fifa World Cup to private investors.

“During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant Fifa governance bodies.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing Fifa Forward programs following the most profitable Fifa World Cup in history was questioned.

“The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance.”

This comes after Uefa’s 55 members, including England, met online and unanimously agreed to boycott ALL Fifa competitions.

Uefa’s scathing statement took aim at Infantino, who has been Fifa’s president for the past ten years.

It read: “This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of Fifa’s duty as the custodian of world football.”



Al-Khelaifi, 52, is viewed as someone that could topple Infantino and is thought to have the backing of leading figures in European football.

He is one of the most powerful people in the game and is the chairman of both beIN Media Group and Qatar Sports Investments.

As well as being president of PSG, the Qatari is chairman of the European Football Clubs and a member of Uefa’s executive committee.

Those backing Al-Khelaifi, however, face an uphill battle in convincing him to stand as a challenger to Infantino.

A spokesperson for Al-Khelaifi told SunSport: “Mr Al-Khelaifi has absolutely no ambition, no intention and no interest in the Fifa role and all this media noise.



Uefa to be tested

“And instead will continue to quietly and constructively support all the institutions of world and European football.”

Uefa’s strong stance against Fifa will be first tested in September, when the Under-20 Women’s World Cup is due to take place.

Six European sides, including England, are due to compete in the tournament that starts on September 5 and is hosted by Poland.

That is just two weeks before the September 19 deadline for countries to accept Infantino’s proposals.

He wants to sell off shares related to Fifa’s commercial and event operations, with the estimation being it could raise £7.52billion.



Fifa member associations will benefit from that and, if they accept the proposed plans, bank £30million.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A chunk of that cash would come in the shape of a £15m lump sum, which would be made available to all 211 members

Countries would then get access to a further £15m over the next three years from 2027 to 2030 via funding.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo sparks weekend wedding rumours after flaunting diamond ring like fiancée Georgina Rodriguez in Majorca
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO Ronaldo flaunts a giant diamond on his ring ­finger like the one he gave Georgina Rodriguez, fuelling talk of a weekend wedding.

The Portuguese footie legend, 42, and Georgina, 32 — mum to three of his six children — both wore their giant sparklers as they boarded a yacht in Majorca.



Local press reported Ron, who proposed with the ring last year, and his missus will get hitched on Saturday.

One TV host claimed the ceremony will be at the Quinta da Regaleira estate in Sintra, Portugal, but it appears to be open to the public this weekend, casting doubt on the claim.





Ronaldo said previously that he and Georgina planned to marry after the World Cup, from which Portugal were ousted by eventual winners Spain.

The striker told Piers Morgan: “I hope to arrive at my wedding with the champion’s trophy.”

He said Georgina was the only woman he had dated that he had wanted to settle down with.

He added: “I’m going to marry her because I believe it’s the right time.



“Not just because she’s the mother of my children — but because she’s the person I love most.”

The pair met in 2016 when model Georgina was working at a Gucci shop in Madrid.



Former Man United hero Ronaldo proposed last August.

He said: “She didn’t care about the ring.

“She asked me if I was speaking the truth.

“She said, ‘Are you honest?’



“And I said, ‘Yes, I’m honest. I want you. I want to marry you’.

“She didn’t believe me at first.”

Georgina shared a snap of the ring, captioned: “I do.”

Sports.title: Bayern Munich beat eighth-tier opposition 15-0 in pre-season friendly as minnows sub on club’s cashier
Sports.content:
BAYERN MUNICH picked up a whopping 15-0 win during a pre-season friendly – but it was their opponents who went viral.

Bayern took on German eighth-tier outfit Rottach-Egern in Bavaria in a friendly that has become the Bundesliga giants’ traditional curtain raiser every year.



Vincent Kompany‘s stars saw the annual game as a formality, but it ended up making more headlines than most of their league games from last season.

That is because Rottach brought on the club’s cashier as a second-half substitute on 79 minutes.



The surprise player, who is reportedly a policeman as well and has been at the club since 2002, took to the pitch against stars like Joshua Kimmich, Jonathan Tah, Joao Palhinha and Kim Min-jae despite his advanced age.

The substitute ran on to the pitch with his team’s colours, while also sporting a dashing moustache.

Fans were left absolutely baffled as they stormed social media.

One tweeted: “Bayern players must have been confused as hell.”

Another commented: “This guy’s about to have the greatest highlight reel of his career even if he doesn’t touch the ball.”

A third wrote: “This should be the most random thing I’ve ever seen.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Another post read: ‘Proper grassroots football, One minute you’re keeping the books, the next you’re coming off the bench.”

Bayern dominated thanks to a brace by Aleksandar Pavlovic, Arijon Ibrahimovic, Felipe Chavez, Maycon Cardozo, Armindo Sieb and Bastian Assomo.

Palhinha, Kimmich and Skender Nuraj also got on the scoresheet. England captain Harry Kane was absent as he’s still on holiday after leading the Three Lions to third place in this summer’s World Cup.

Sports.title: Ex-Newcastle chief Amanda Staveley close to buying stake in West Ham after being spotted at London Stadium
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY is close to buying a stake in West Ham.

The ex-Newcastle director, alongside her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, is leading a consortium set to buy the Gold family’s 25.1% stake in the Hammers.



Staveley, who led the Saudi Toon takeover, is reported to have backing from US and Far East-based investors.

She was spotted at the London Stadium in June, attending Take That‘s Circus Tour with her husband.



SunSport understands the pair were guests of the venue rather than West Ham themselves, and were sat in the directors’ box.

The Times reports the Staveley-led consortium hopes to restore West Ham’s Premier League status and could even buy the London Stadium.

Their plan would also include ‘significant’ transfer investment, hoping to revive the club’s fortunes after a dismal 2025/26 season saw them relegated to the Championship.

Any Staveley investment remains subject to a ‘pre-emption process’, which means existing shareholders would get first refusal on buying the shares.

Among those shareholders is Czech tycoon Daniel Kretinsky, who holds a 43% stake in the club.

Royal Mail owner Kretinsky is set to become the majority shareholder, after last month striking a deal to buy a further 16% in the Hammers from the Gold family.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The deal, however, is yet to be ratified.

David Sullivan remains the largest shareholder as it stands, with a 38.8% stake, though he could be forced to sell up with the independent football regulator investigating his position following allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.

Sullivan, 77, denies all allegations and resigned to fight them.

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘discuss Igor Thiago transfer’ with Red Devils looking to add competition for Benjamin Sesko
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are keeping tabs on Brentford star Igor Thiago as they look to add significant firepower to their frontline, reports suggest.

Michael Carrick has been focusing on midfield additions during the summer with the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, while also eyeing further targets.



According to transfer insider Ben Jacobs, however, Man Utd are also looking to reinforce their attack ahead of a demanding season that will see them challenging domestically and in Europe.

Jacobs revealed the Red Devils are weighing up a swoop for Thiago, 25, after a stunning campaign that saw him finishing as the Premier League’s second top scorer.



The striker amassed a whopping 22 goals in 38 appearances – just five less than Manchester City superstar Erling Haaland.

United have even contacted the Brazil international’s camp but negotiations are still at an early stage.



And it will be “incredibly difficult” convincing Brentford to sell their star asset.

Jacobs told The United Stand: “Igor Thiago has been discussed, somebody that’s Premier League ready.

“Nothing more than that at this stage, more of an internal conversation and a normal player call to understand his situation.

“Getting him out this summer will be incredibly difficult.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Thiago amassed 25 goals and one assist in 40 appearances across all competitions last season.

The Brazilian would add tremendous competition for Benjamin Sesko, who registered a total of 12 goals and one assist in 32 appearances in his debut year with United.

Sesko, 23, mostly operated as an impact player off the bench under Carrick and is currently nursing a shin injury.

And Joshua Zirkzee’s future at Old Trafford is uncertain as he attracts interest from the Serie A with Juventus posing as favourites for his signature.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho training next to Man Utd HQ at ground of 10th tier minnows who are coached by Reds’ icon’s brother
Sports.content:
JADON SANCHO has been training at 10th tier minnows Flixton FC – just a stone’s throw away from Manchester United’s training ground.

Sancho is now a free agent after his Old Trafford nightmare officially ended this summer, calling time on years of endless loan spells.



The 26-year-old winger, whom United splashed £73m on in 2021, has been using upgraded non-league facilities at Flixton’s 2,000-capacity Valley Road ground.

In a club interview, Sancho said: “You’ve got a nice layout here. It’s the first time I’ve seen a nice pitch [in this area] apart from United and City.”



Flixton are gearing up for their first competitive season since going bust in 2012, having been brought back from the dead by a new investor last year.

United legend Ryan Giggs‘ estranged brother Rhodri Giggs, who previously managed Salford City, was appointed as assistant manager last summer.



The cash investment in the facilities comes after American financier Christopher Garcia, CEO of US based Wilshire Quinn Capital, purchased the club in February 2025.

Originally opened by Sir Alex Ferguson back in 1995, Flixton’s Valley Road ground had been reduced to hosting Sunday League games before being slapped with a £500,000 price tag on Rightmove in January 2025.

While weighing up his next options, Sancho promised he’d be in the stands to watch Flixton play next Tuesday, just a ten-minute drive away from Carrington.

The London-born forward has drawn interest from Qatari club Al Rayyan and has been previously targeted by Roma in Serie A.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sancho spent the past three seasons on loan at Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa, achieving the remarkable feat of playing in a European final for all three – all in different competitions.

He won the Europa League with Villa but failed to find the consistency that once made him one of Europe’s most sought-after young players.

The former England winger, who came through City and Watford’s youth ranks, played just 83 matches for United before his public row with former boss Erik ten Hag in 2023.

Villa have since signed ex-United star Alejandro Garnacho on a season-long loan from Chelsea to fill the void on the left wing.

Sports.title: 'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'
Sports.content:
'Gianni Infantino should resign from FIFA now — or football will suffer forever'

Gianni Infantino, the president of FIFA since 2016, was on Thursday accused of "putting profit ahead of fans" amid the controversial plans to sell stakes of the World Cup

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has become a danger to the game he was elected to protect. His proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors would reduce football’s greatest tournament to a financial asset, carved up by people interested in profit rather than passion. England will not take part. Neither will France, Germany, Spain, Italy or Europe’s other leading nations. They are right to threaten a boycott and must stand firm. Without Europe, the World Cup would be a sham: a gutted tournament missing many of its greatest teams, rivalries and supporters. Infantino knows this, yet he has still offered national associations £30 million to back his scheme. That is no way to run world football. It is an attempt to buy compliance while selling off the game’s crown jewels. The Mirror says Infantino has forfeited the right to lead FIFA. He should resign now. If he will not, he must be removed before his greed leaves football permanently poorer.

‌



Fires no freak

For weeks, Britain has watched in horror as wildfires tore through Europe. Now our own countryside is alight. More than 100 firefighters are battling flames across Suffolk heathland covering an area the size of 140 football pitches, while families have been forced from caravans and holiday parks. Their courage is extraordinary, as is the kindness of neighbours opening their homes to evacuees and their pets. Yet this cannot be dismissed as a freak disaster. We are heating the planet, drying the land and creating the conditions in which fires spread faster and burn harder. Andy Burnham must give crews every resource they need. But, despite the deniers, we all must act on the climate crisis with the urgency it demands. Europe’s nightmare is reaching our shores. Without change, this terrifying summer will become the new normal.

Ace in the old

At 100, Ivor Parker has finally turned a lifelong poker hobby into a job. After 86 years at the tables, he has been signed as the world’s oldest paid professional. His secret is patience, nerve and knowing when to hold ’em. Retirement, clearly, was never really on the cards.

It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plans have been met with fury by UEFA members (Image: AFP or licensors)

“It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

‌



“National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process.

“The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

“This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

‌



“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

“Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

Article continues below

“Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola handed Liverpool setback as injury blow confirmed
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola handed Liverpool setback as injury blow confirmed

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola already has another injury to deal with after the team failed to come through this summer's first pre-season friendly against Sunderland unscathed

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola will be without the injured Joe Gomez for around a month (Image: ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Joe Gomez sustained a muscle injury during Liverpool's first pre-season friendly against Sunderland. The Reds' head coach believes "it will be impossible" to have him available for the start of the Premier League season.

‌



Gomez, 29, lasted just eight minutes of the match in Nashville before having to be substituted. Ifeanyi Ndukwe replaced Liverpool's longest-serving player, who handed the captain's armband over to Kostas Tsimikas, who has returned from a loan at Roma this summer.

‌



The former England international was absent from their match overnight against Wrexham. Gomez now faces a month on the sidelines.

‌



Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool READ MORE :

Iraola offered an injury update on Thursday during a press conference in Chicago: "Joe has a muscle injury. It was quite clear since he complained straight away, so he will be off for some weeks.

"It's a muscle injury. It's difficult to say - normally one month. If it goes very well, then a little bit less. If it goes bad, then a bit more, but it's a muscle injury.

"It's not massive. I think it will be impossible to have him at the start of the season because we are not that far, but it shouldn't be much more."

‌



View 2 Images Joe Gomez is due to be missing for the next month with a muscle injury (Image: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

"You've seen in these games that we are pretty thin in the centre-back position. We still don't have Virgil [van Dijk]. The only centre-backs we have right now are Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who are 18, have just arrived at the club and are doing incredibly well.

"Yesterday, Luke Chambers played there - he's not a centre-back, but he played really well. Until we recover some bodies - I think Jeremy [Jacquet] is ready to go."

‌



Iraola continued: "A lot of players have surprised me, especially the young players I did not know before. The senior players, you have played against them and know them.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"The young players have given a very, very high level in these friendlies. They have to grow, which is very good. We will recover players; it would not be good if we played against Newcastle the same 11 we did yesterday.

Article continues below

"Important players we will get back, they have been at the World Cup. We have done a great job with these players in the first two weeks, and then we have to integrate the new ones slowly. These players know where we are going and can help us."

Sports.title: Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest caught out as Premier League gambling ban bites
Sports.content:
Three Premier League teams are poised to start the 2026/27 season without front-of-shirt sponsors after falling to navigate the market in the wake of a ban on gambling companies.

It was way back in April 2023 when Premier League clubs agreed to get rid of gambling companies on the front of their shirts. And yet Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest have so far been unable to find a suitable replacement.

Obscure gambling companies had become part of the furniture of elite football, delighted to pay millions to for brand exposure - often in markets where gambling is illegal. Premier League sides were more than happy to accept their money - often worth double the offers from non-gambling companies - despite ethical concerns.

After mounting pressure, including from the government, that came to an end this summer. Eleven of the 20 teams in the Premier League last season had a gambling company emblazoned on their shirt. Three of those were relegated, leaving eight teams that needed to find a replacement this summer.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

Arsenal close in on £80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer in major breakthrough for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Six have been successful, but alongside Chelsea - who have had their own sponsor struggles in recent years - Sunderland and Forest look set to go sponsor-less 22 days before the season kicks off. Inside the commercial teams of Premier League clubs, gambling sponsors had been viewed as too good to turn down. They paid more than other companies and wanted less in return, acting as a simple billboard to millions of viewers.

While Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brentford, Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham managed to secure new sponsors, likely on reduced rates, Sunderland and Forest have held out. Sean Connell, editor of The Sponsor, an independent sponsorship research and valuation publication, believes they have become victim of " the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment" in Premier League history. In short, commercial teams have been forced to do more work for less reward.

"It’s an incredibly competitive sponsorship market," he tells Mirror Football. "The number of brands willing to put their hands in their pocket and stump up £5m to £15m to sponsor a Premier League club is already significantly reduced due to factors outside the sports landscape.

‌



View 4 Images Sunderland have gone from gambling company W88 to no sponsor (Image: Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images)

"Sponsors are under incredible amount of scrutiny to justify their expenditure. Then there's an unusually high number of teams in the market looking for a sponsor – in a normal year it might only be one or two, but it was 11 this summer.

"The gambling ban has taken what was already a shrinking pool of sponsors and removed a healthy chunk of those. It’s created what I believe is the most competitive and difficult sponsorship environment that Premier League clubs have ever faced."

The gambling ban has been looming for over three years and Connell believes some have been guilty of failing to burying their heads in the sand. Mirror Football contacted Chelsea, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest to request comment.

‌



Premier League front-of-shirt sponsors 2026/27 Arsenal – Emirates (Airline) Aston Villa – Visit Rwanda (Tourism) Bournemouth – Vitality (Insurance) Brentford – Indeed (Employment) Brighton – American Express (Bank) Chelsea – NONE Coventry – Monzo (Bank) Crystal Palace – Temporal (Software platform) Everton – CMC Markets (Financial services) Fulham – ClickHouse (Technology) Hull City – Corendon Airlines (Airline) Ipswich – Halo (Software) Leeds – Red Bull (Drinks) Liverpool – Standard Chartered (Bank) Manchester City – Etihad Airways (Airline) Manchester United – Snapdragon (Electronics) Newcastle – Knox (Sports drinks) Nottingham Forest – NONE (previously Bally’s) Sunderland – NONE (previously W88) Tottenham – AIA (Insurance)

“The profits and revenue have been so much greater than they would have been that nobody has taken any meaningful strides to address this," Connell says. "They have continued to take the money while the sun shone. Now some like Forest and Sunderland are in a difficult position.

“I think the clubs have been waiting to see what the highest possible deal is at the last possible moment. For some clubs that strategy worked out, for others like Sunderland and Forest they have presumably determined that the value of the deal on the table is not adequate and that holding out rather than underselling is the best strategy.”

Chelsea's situation is different. Remarkably, the Blues have not had a permanent front‑of‑shirt sponsor since their deal with Three ended in 2023. In February they announced a front-of-shirt deal until the end of the season with AI technology company IFS, but are now once again sponsor-less.

‌



View 4 Images Nottingham Forest have been unable to replace their gambling sponsor (Image: Gualter Fatia/Getty Images)

It has been reported that Chelsea have been holding out for £65m per season for their front-of-shirt sponsorship. Yet their 10th-place finish, and failure to secure any European football next season, appears to have damaged their chances.

While the gambling ban has undoubtedly impacted the revenues of Premier League clubs, particularly those outside the elite, who have more pulling power, it is a landmark moment in the league. R esearch in 2023 found that betting logos appear up to 3,500 times during TV games, a troubling reality for vulnerable people and gambling addicts.

Will Prochaska, director of the Coalition to End Gambling Ads (CEGA), said: “Andy Burnham has said we should 'relegate gambling sponsorship of sport to the history books' and we agree.

‌



View 4 Images Gambling sponsors had been ubiquitous in the Premier League (Image: Mark Fletcher/Getty Images)

“Fans will have little sympathy with clubs struggling to replace front-of-shirt gambling sponsors, and there's more than enough money in the game to ensure football can thrive without gambling revenues.

“Formula 1 cried foul that ending tobacco sponsorship would destroy the sport, but it's gone from strength to strength. Ridding football of its links to the gambling sector is an opportunity to turn a corner, not a burden.”

While gambling companies are still allowed on the sleeves of shirts in the Premier League, the gambling gold rush, when millions flowed into the game from obscure gambling entities operating via “white label” agreements with a company in the Isle of Man, are over. The results will be obvious come the first weekend of the season.

‌

Sports.title: 'No Plan B': Will Matthias Jaissle have tactical flexibility Eddie Howe never showed at Newcastle?
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United manager, bringing to a close a hugely successful five-year spell in which the former Bournemouth boss took the Magpies back into the Champions League and ended a 56-year wait for a trophy by beating Liverpool in the EFL Cup final.

However, Howe increasingly faced criticism for not developing a successful 'Plan B' to his brand of high-intensity, physical football, which saw results suffer when fatigue, the demand of European football, and injuries impacted his first-choice team.

AI 'supercomputer' Machine Football's analysis of the manager widely expected to take over from Howe, current Al Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle, shows how his style of play has evolved over time and could be just what Newcastle need to once again instil a clear identity.

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

How Jaissle's style has evolved

2023/24:

‌



Jaissle's first Al Ahli side were what Machine Football categorises as 'high-octane pressers', setting up for the majority of games in a 4-2-3-1 formation and relying heavily on dribbling and forward carries alongside an aggressive press.

That approach delivered 1.85 points per game and continental qualification. But Jaissle did not stop there, evolving his side further ahead of the following season.

2024/25:

Al Ahli developed into what Machine Football categorises as 'aggressive disruptors', with the emphasis shifting away from wing play and towards creating higher-quality chances with expected goals rising from 1.59 per 90 to 1.97 and points per game increasing to 2.04.

‌



Your Machine Football glossary of football tactics, data and stats buzzwords READ MORE :

2025/26:

Next, Jaissle added flexibility without changing the identity. Alongside the primary 4-2-3-1 setup - which he used in more than 40% of games - the German introduced a 4-3-3 variation in 22% of his games and, in roughly one match out of every five, more of a low-block counter style of play built on a traditional 4-4-2.

While the formations may have varied, the approach didn't. Al Ahli's PPDA (presses per defensive action - a pressing measurement where the lower the score, the more aggressive the press) was a high-octane 9.02.

Al Ahli also averaged 7.18 through passes per game – well above the Saudi Pro League average of 4.13 – and 19.83 touches inside the opposition box, comfortably ahead of the league average of 16.46.

‌



Rather than dominating possession, Al Ahli look to win the ball high and attack quickly. That approach resulted in Jaissle's best domestic season yet, averaging 2.38 points per game while winning a second consecutive AFC Champions League Elite title.

View 4 Images Cohesion: Newcastle v Al Ahli (2025/26). Al Ahli's weaker connections between defensive and midfield lines reflects their preference for vertical passes rather than slow build-up (Image: Machine Football)

Howe's 'flip-flopping' tactical approach

Who Jaissle is tactically suggests a significant change from the Newcastle side he looks set to inherit. The contrast becomes clearer when the numbers are put side by side.

The perception that Howe never managed to successfully implement a 'Plan B' comes from a run of seasons where the club's fortunes flip-flopped. Newcastle's style clearly changed from season to season during his tenure at St James' Park, but results also yo-yo'd.

‌



In 2022/23 Newcastle were what Machine Football's analysis classes as 'high-octane pressers' and enjoyed their best-ever points return (2.09 PPG).

The 2023/24 season, however, saw Champions League group stage football return and a shift towards a 'passive controllers' model accompany it.

In practice, Newcastle were playing more patient, lower-tempo football focused on control. It was still productive (1.72 PPG) but represented a step down in intensity and earned only a seventh placed Premier League finish.

In 2024/25 - no European football again - Howe swung back toward a more progressive, 'attacking engine' playing style. This helped their PPG bounce back up to 1.81 resulting in fifth place and Champions League qualification for a second time under Howe.

‌



Another flip then followed in 2025-26 as they moved into 'possession builders' - the most control-oriented identity of the four seasons - but only in just over half of their games, as PPG (1.26) reached its lowest ebb of any of Howe's four full seasons and Newcastle stuttered to 12th place in the league.

What this topsy-turvy playing identity suggests is that the new manager's style could help the Magpies get back to something like the best version of themselves from 22/23.

View 4 Images Stats comparison of Newcastle and Al Ahli 2025/26: Note how despite taking fewer shots, Al Ahli had a higher percentage of their efforts hit the target and a higher xG per 90 (Image: Machine Football)

Taking the stats from 2025-26, Newcastle and Al Ahli's possession is almost identical, but everything that follows is different. Last season, Al Ahli completed around 80 fewer passes per game - yet attempted more than twice as many through balls, created higher-quality chances and conceded almost half as many goals.

‌



Jaissle's style, then, is built entirely around progressing the ball quickly and attacking before opponents can reset.

Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier READ MORE :

Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit READ MORE :

Can Saudi success translate to Premier League?

While the change in approach might seem drastic, it looks set to get the Gallowgate End on its feet and - most importantly - the underlying numbers suggest it could translate into results, albeit with star players continuing to depart Newcastle.

Across 34 Saudi Pro League matches, Al Ahli scored 71 goals (2.09 per game), conceded just 25 (0.74 per game), kept 17 clean sheets and won 73.5% of their league matches.

Their expected goals total (66.73) closely mirrored their actual return, suggesting the attacking output is sustainable rather than the product of an unusually clinical season.

‌



View 4 Images A possible best XI for Jaissle's Newcastle based on the current options available (Image: Machine Football)

Newcastle's numbers tell a different story. They scored 53 goals in 38 Premier League games (1.39 per game), won just 36.8% of their matches and finished with expected goals for and against that were almost identical (59.23 xG versus 59.5 xGA).

The difference isn't how much of the ball the two teams have. It's what they do with it. Now all that's left is for Jaissle to prove he can make the same principles work in the Premier League.

‌
