He said that a unified coordinated mechanism be put in place for regular monitoring of all the developments to ensure expeditious implementation of appropriate measures to safeguard the interests of the citizens.â

World.title: Supreme Court: No blanket ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed Delhi government to provide treatment to those injured during studentsâ protests but found a plea for ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control vague and asked when police are permitted to fire bullets in extreme situations, how could pellet guns be banned.

Appearing for petitioners, advocate Vrinda Grover questioned the legality of Rapid Action Force using pellet guns against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar, and urged the SC to direct the Union govt to preserve the ammunition log of RAF during their deployment at the protest site and award exemplary compensation to those injured by metallic pellets.

The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20, and former IPS officer Yashovardhan Azad.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed preservation of the logbook, and solicitor general Tushar Mehta said all documents required for an effective investigation into alleged police excesses and violence at the protest site would be preserved.

Both protesters and police human beings: Supreme Court

When Grover persisted with the plea for a ban on use of pellet guns, Justice Bagchi termed the prayer vague and said, âPolice regulations permit use of pellet guns in exceptional circumstances.





If you want phasing out of pellet guns, then you must challenge those regulations, which you have not done.

âYou say at no stage metallic pellet can be used, when graded response permits use of bullets in extreme situations. Seeking ban on use of pellet guns cannot be on the same plane as seeking a ban on use of bullets (for crowd dispersal)? Law permits use of bullets.â

Justice Bagchi recalled a Calcutta High Court order quashing a colonial-era police regulation asking personnel to fire at chests instead of legs of protesters to save ammunition.

The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for policeâs graded action delineating when to use rubber pellets followed by metallic pellets. Grover agreed to amend the prayer to enable the SC to provide guidelines for the policeâs crowd dispersal action.

The bench reiterated that there were occasions when peaceful protests were hijacked by miscreants and became vehicles for ulterior purposes, including for the purpose of sabotaging the bona fide aim of the protests.

âAll such situations would require various graded responses. But most important is to equip police with adequate safety gear. Only then can they ponder over graded responses to violent crowds. Otherwise, the protesters and police, both are human beings and react equally to threats coming to them,â the bench said. The SG said citizens always have a right to non-violent protest.

Grover said updated guidelines framed by Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPRD) were not available after 2016 and it was very difficult to obtain information from police.

The bench said this was not correct and such guidelines should be uploaded on websites. The SG said he would check the veracity of Azadâs allegation.

The SC had said on July 28 that it was prima facie convinced about a high-level inquiry into alleged police excesses and violence against cops and directed police to preserve data collected from various cameras but restrained them from taking coercive action against students and making public their personal data.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Grover said petitioners Mansoori and Singh were injured by metallic pellets fired by RAF without provocation. She said while Mansoori received good treatment at Lady Hardinge Hospital, Singh did not, leading the SC to direct Delhi govt to provide adequate treatment to the two and all those injured during the protests led by CJP.

World.title: Naveen Patnaik lambasts BJP government for changing Indian Hockey jersey colour from blue to saffron
World.content:
Former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik, considered one of the patrons of Indian Hockey during his rule, expressed deep anguish over the reported change of colour of the Indian hockey team’s jersey from blue to saffron.

Hailed for being instrumental in making Odisha the sponsor of Indian hockey when it was struggling for support, Mr. Patnaik on Thursday (July 30, 2026) condemned the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Odisha for allegedly politicising a national game like hockey in an emotional post on X.

“It has deeply hurt the sentiments of lakhs of sports lovers across the country and the pride with which Odisha has supported the national hockey,” said former Odisha CM.

“I am deeply anguished to know that the legendary colour of the Indian hockey team’s jersey has been changed to saffron. The iconic shade of blue of the Indian hockey team is not just a colour. It is an emotion associated with the nation’s sporting heritage,” said the veteran politician.

He said, “For decades, this colour united us in hope, in victory, in defeat and in the pursuit of sporting excellence. We have cried, laughed, celebrated and stood proudly with our men and women in blue. Wearing the blue jersey, our teams have won Olympic medals with the national anthem playing on the world stage.”

Stating that blue is derived from the blue chakra in our national flag, he pointed out that “it is a symbol of our national pride and identity. The colour blue belongs to every Indian.”

“When the national hockey teams were struggling for sponsors, Odisha created history by being the first and only State to support our national teams and our beloved game. Every Odia across the globe was proud of the State’s gift to national hockey. After 41 long years, our men’s team won an Olympic medal. Just because the government changed in Odisha, it should not change our national team colours,” observed former CM and now Leader of Opposition in Odisha Legislative Assembly.

Charging that this is petty politics of the worst kind, Mr. Patnaik said, “Our blue jersey is to us what the iconic stripes are to Argentina, and the yellow jersey is to Brazil. It is etched in our collective memory. Any change in this colour, is a crass attempt to erase our priceless sporting legacy.”

“National symbols are meant to unite us, not divide. I am given to understand that this step was taken under pressure from the BJP government in Odisha. Those in authority may deny it, but the fact is that for the last two years, everybody in Odisha has seen the obsession of this government with changing colours of buildings, buses and even bridges,” he added.

World.title: Despite Centre’s assurance, people still being called to explain their presence at protest site, says member of Congress’ legal aid
World.content:
Days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called off its agitation at Jantar Mantar, protesters continued to be summoned by the Delhi Police until Thursday (July 30, 2026) afternoon to explain their presence at the protest site, according to Rishav Ranjan, a member of the Congress party’s legal cell who has been involved in providing legal aid.

Later in the day, the Delhi government issued an order withdrawing all cases against the protesters, in line with an assurance given by Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh during a meeting with a two-member CJP delegation on July 25.

Mr. Ranjan said that a helpline launched by the party has so far received 300 calls, including 50 calls by young girls and women who were being issued rape and death threats for participating in the protests.

He said the Supreme Court’s July 28 order directing the immediate release of all minors arrested in connection with the demonstrations and restraining the police from taking coercive action against protesting students without criminal antecedents was not being implemented.

“The withdrawal of FIRs is effective only in Bihar, especially not in Delhi. The threats by the State not to join the protest and not to do politics around the students’ issue continue. Today, three individuals from Haryana were brought to the Parliament Street police station for questioning without any notice. One of them was blindfolded and brought here; when we intervened, he was let off near the Karnal by-pass around 3.30 pm by the police,” Mr. Ranjan said.

Caught on camera: on the use of force at Jantar Mantar

He added that he was working in tandem with the CJP legal team, and other independent lawyers were also helping the detained persons.

He said despite the assurance by the Central government, juveniles were released from Bhagalpur in Bihar and Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) night, and there were several others who were yet to be released.

As the interim Supreme Court order permitted the authorities to proceed with the investigation of the existing FIRs, the police in some States are acting arbitrarily under its guise, he said.

“Many girls are getting calls from right-wing influencers asking why they joined the protest. Their names are part of a list, which is being circulated by these handles. They are being harassed and threatened. There is clear evidence online. This needs serious action by the State,” he said, adding that the Supreme Court will be informed about such incidents.

A delegation also plans to meet the Delhi Police Commissioner.

“We need to seriously lodge FIRs to help these women. They need urgent guidance and protection. The State has to take an action and make an example out of them,” he added.

He said there were apprehensions that the detentions and instances of people being summoned for questioning at police stations were based on images captured by Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras installed at the protest site.

World.title: Parliament passes paper leak Bill as Opposition walks out of Rajya Sabha
World.content:
Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, after the Rajya Sabha too cleared it on Thursday. The Lok Sabha had passed the Bill on Wednesday. Opposition members belonging to the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) walked out of the House before the reply by Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Jitendra Singh to the seven-hour debate. The Upper House considered the Bill after the government listed it as supplementary agenda.

Also read | Rajya Sabha adjourned twice as Opposition demands Amit Shah’s presence over protest crackdown

Replying to the debate, Mr. Singh questioned the Opposition’s contention that there have been 152 examination paper leaks under the Narendra Modi government. “They could not authenticate it,” he said, adding that the government has made efforts to free medical education from management quota malice. He said the government had increased the number of All India Institutes of Medical Sciences and both undergraduate and post-graduate seats in medical education. He said the government’s approach lays emphasis on democratisation of education. “The National Education Policy has liberated children from the slavery of subjects chosen by their parents, teachers or guardians,” he said.

Earlier, moving the Bill, Mr. Singh said the Bill reflects the Union government’s commitment to safeguard the interests of students and youth while ensuring merit, consistency, transparency and credibility in the public examination system. “The objective of the legislation is to ensure greater consistency, credibility and transparency in public examinations so that sincere and deserving candidates are rewarded for their genuine efforts and their future is not jeopardised by organised examination-related crimes,” he said.

Initiating the debate, Opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge demanded a Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee probe into the NEET paper leaks and the police action on protesters. He demanded the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and warned that people’s power will drag him “out of his forts” and make him answerable for what the government was doing against the students. “You are the Home Minister, and despite so much unrest, you are not opening your mouth. Has someone stitched it? He should have spoken openly. In the interest of the nation, he should have borne that insult,” he said.

Criticising the intention of the government, he said the Bill was much delayed and does not address how to prevent paper leaks. He said question papers for 152 State and Central examinations were leaked in the last 10 years and and no one has ever been punished for the crime.

“After pressure due to nationwide protests by youth, for the first time in 12 years, the Education Minister has resigned. The Higher Education Secretary was transferred. The government claimed to have removed 47 officials of the NTA (National Testing Agency),” Mr. Kharge said, and added that more than 30 lakh posts are lying vacant across the country but the Centre does not want to fill the vacancies as a majority of those posts would have gone to Dalits, Adivasis and Backward Classes.

Congress MP Mukul Wasnik pointed to the systemic issues in the holding of examinations and urged the government to take the matter seriously. Trinamool Congress’s Sagarika Ghose too demanded Mr. Shah’s resignation. “I demand that the Home Minister come to this House, make a statement, answer the students, apologise to the students. If he cannot do so, the Home Minister must resign,” she said. Rashtriya Janata Dal MP Manoj Jha and Samajwadi Party MP Ramgopal Yadav demanded that the NTA be dismantled. Communist Party of India (Marxist) member John Brittas said the government was not treating the root cause of the issue, which was commercialisation of education. The DMK did not walk out with India bloc members, but moved amendments against the Bill, which were defeated.

World.title: Woman arrested with hasish oil in Kerala’s Kozhikode
World.content:
The Kozhikode City police on Thursday arrested a 32-year-old woman after recovering 56 grams of hashish oil from her during a surprise inspection at the Government Medical College Hospital here.

The accused, identified as Aswathi from Wayanad who is currently residing in Kasaragod, had reportedly come to the hospital as a bystander for a patient admitted to the maternity ward.

According to the police, the contraband was concealed in two small plastic bottles. Hospital staff and caregivers in the ward reportedly became suspicious of the woman’s behaviour and alerted the police, leading to the inspection and seizure.

Police officials attached to the Kozhikode Medical College station said the woman was attempting to smuggle the cannabis extract to her husband, who is lodged in the Kozhikode district jail. Investigators found that she intended to pass the substance to other inmates who were brought to the Medical College Hospital, from where it could eventually reach the prison.

A case was registered, and an investigation is under way to trace the source of the drug. The police said they had intensified surveillance to prevent attempts to supply narcotic substances to prisoners through hospitals or other transit points.

World.content:
The live blog is closed

The United States military launched “powerful” strikes on Iran on Thursday (July 30, 2026), in retaliation for Tehran’s attacks targeting U.S. bases in Jordan as the war in West Asia reignited and again drew in the Islamic republic’s proxies. “The strikes are a powerful response to yesterday’s attempted Iranian attacks on U.S. forces”, U.S. Central Command said.

Despite several days of relative calm, both sides carried out military strikes in the last 24 hours that once again risk a return to all-out war — and further expansion in the region — while little is clear about what strategy, if any, American or Iranian officials have for a path forward.

Iran’s state television, meanwhile, reported a U.S. strike in the Piranshahr border area, after the Fars news agency reported a missile hit an uninhabited area, causing no casualties. Earlier, Jordan’s army said it had intercepted five Iranian missiles, with Iran’s Revolutionary Guards saying they had targeted U.S. bases there.

World.title: Opposition protests police action against students, Ram temple donations
World.content:
Stepping up its attack on the Narendra Modi government over alleged police excesses against students protesting the NEET paper leak and alleged chadhawa chori (donation theft) at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, Opposition MPs on Thursday (July 30, 2026) staged a protest at the Makar Dwar, the main entrance to the Parliament House.

Congress general secretaries K C Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party’s Dharmendra Yadav, Trinamool Congress’s Sagarika Ghose and Jharkhand Mukti Morcha’s Mahua Maji were among those who participated.

The MPs raised slogans including “chadhawa chor, gaddi chor”, “Grih Mantri sadan mein aao” [Home Minister come to the House] and “who gave the order?”, demanding an explanation for the use of force against protesting students.

They also carried a large banner reading “Who gave the order?” and displayed a donation box, into which they placed money to symbolically highlight their allegations regarding temple donations.

In a post on X, Mr. Venugopal questioned the absence of Home Minister Amit Shah from Parliament, referring to him as “MIA (missing in action)”, and asked who had ordered the use of pellet guns against students. He also alleged that the government had prevented Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi from speaking in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday (July 29, 2026).

Political statements and allegations

Opposition leaders used the protest to press for answers on both issues, with several MPs accusing the government of failing to provide clarity on the police response to student demonstrations. The protest was also used to reiterate allegations of irregularities in the management of donations at the Ram temple, which the MPs said required investigation and accountability.

Mamata’s Congress history and a reply from Priyanka Gandhi

The space outside Makar Dwar also saw a sharp exchange between Ms Vadra and suspended Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee, who was holding a separate demonstration over his suspension.

Mr. Banerjee was wearing a poster displaying photographs of 20 TMC MPs he described as “traitors from Bengal”. Seeing the poster, a visibly amused Ms. Vadra told the suspended Trinamool MP leaders that many of them had left the Congress to join the TMC.

Mr Banerjee told Ms. Vadra that the Congress would not be in its current position had Mamata Banerjee not been expelled from the party in 1997.

Responding to his remarks, Ms. Vadra recalled that former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi had extended “love and respect” to Ms. Banerjee during her time in the Congress.

Mr. Banerjee countered that the Congress’s later decision to align with the CPI(M) in West Bengal had created divisions between Ms. Banerjee and the party.

World.title: Narcotics Control Bureau busts pan-India LSD distribution network
World.content:
CHENNAI

In a breakthrough against courier-based narcotics trafficking, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), through a coordinated inter-zonal operation involving its Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Kochi Zonal Units, said it dismantled a sophisticated pan-India Lysergic Acid Diethylamide (LSD) distribution network that was operating under the cover of express courier services.

The agency said the probe commenced with the seizure of LSD blots in Chennai. Investigation into the backward linkages and supply chain revealed that parcels containing LSD were being dispatched from Pune to various parts of the country through courier services.

Based on sustained intelligence and technical surveillance, NCB officers conducted a week-long coordinated operation in Chennai, Kanniyakumari and Pune. The operation resulted in the arrest of a key syndicate member responsible for receiving, repackaging and dispatching LSD consignments to customers across multiple States.

The accused was intercepted while preparing consignments for dispatch to Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. The parcels were seized before they could reach their intended destinations.

Subsequent searches led to the recovery of substantial quantities of LSD and other narcotic substances from the residence of the accused.

Doctor and medico among accused

Further investigation resulted in the seizure of two parcels destined for Tamil Nadu and the arrest of three accused, including a doctor and a medical college student.

One of the intercepted parcels contained 225 LSD blots planned for distribution in Kodaikanal. Two persons allegedly managing guest houses in Kodaikanal and suspected to be associated with the syndicate were presently absconding, and efforts were on to apprehend them.

During the operation, NCB officers seized 2,796 LSD blots, 166 grams of a greenish substance suspected to be Hydroponic Ganja, 113 Nitrazepam tablets weighing 59.89 grams and Rs 70,000 in cash, suspected to be proceeds of illicit drug trafficking.

Investigation revealed the narcotic substances trafficked by the syndicate were sourced through a darknet marketplace, where a vendor operating a dedicated personalised vendor storefront was offering LSD for sale to buyers across India.

The vendor, accepted payments in Monero (XMR) a privacy-oriented cryptocurrency specifically designed to obscure transaction trails, in order to defeat financial tracing and conceal the movement of illicit proceeds.

The use of encrypted messaging platforms in combination with anonymity-focused cryptocurrencies and reshipping arrangements reflects an increasingly layered operational model adopted by narcotics networks to insulate principal suppliers from detection.

Efforts are under way to establish the identity of the operator behind the darknet vendor profile and to trace the associated cryptocurrency transactions, in coordination with relevant agencies.

The NCB said in a press release that the syndicate dispatched at least 14 parcels from April 2026 onwards, indicating the existence of a well-organised and sustained interstate drug trafficking network.

“LSD is a potent hallucinogenic drug that poses serious mental and psychological health risks, including hallucinations, anxiety, tremors, depression and other behavioural disturbances. NCB has observed that LSD is frequently concealed inside documents, books, greeting cards and similar articles to evade detection during transit,” the agency said.

The central drug law-enforcement agency urged courier and logistics service providers to remain vigilant and implement stringent Know Your Customer (KYC) norms to prevent the misuse of courier channels for narcotics trafficking.

World.title: Calcutta HC seeks report from police over ‘encounter killing’ of Baruipur rape-murder accused
World.content:
The Calcutta High Court on Thursday sought a detailed report from the Baruipur district police in connection with the “encounter killing” of Prabhash Mondal, the main accused in the rape and murder of a minor girl.

A Division Bench of Justices Tapabrata Chakraborty and Partha Sarathi Chattopadhyay passed the order while hearing a public interest litigation plea filed by advocate Shiladitya Rakshit. It claimed that the police’s statements in connection with the “encounter killing” were “fabricated”.

Around 12.45 a.m. on July 8, a team from the Baruipur police station took the accused to the encounter spot for the reconstruction of the crime scene.

The police said the accused allegedly snatched the service weapon of a police officer, fired one round at the police team, and attempted to flee.

Prima facie, the autopsy report found two bullets in the body of the accused fired by Inspector Arghya Mondal, officials said.

Preliminary investigation into the rape and murder case suggested that the accused had abducted the girl and raped her before throwing her into a pond, according to officials. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the crime after the 12-year-old girl’s body was fished out of a pond on July 5 in Baruipur, South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. The incident sparked a violent protest in the area, with an angry mob killing a person over suspicion of his involvement in the crime.

Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya told the court that the police failed to arrange sufficient security measures at the reconstruction site that led to the mishap. He also questioned the timing of the crime reconstruction late at night amid adverse weather conditions.

Advocate General Rajdeep Majumder argued that the police had to shoot in self-defence. He said the police also registered a suo motu FIR and the matter is being probed by the Criminal Investigation Department. The case will be heard again on August 18.

World.title: Seema Kaliramna, PhD and mother of 3-year-old, wins CWG 2026 discus bronze
World.content:
Seema Kaliramna recorded a best throw of 58.65m to clinch the bronze medal in the women’s Discus throw at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow.

Competing in a field that had previous edition’s medallist Obiageri Amaechi of Nigeria, World Championships finalist Samantha Hall of Jamaica and Julia Tunks of Canada, Seema recorded only two legal throws but that was enough for her to finish on the third spot.



Hall won the gold medal with 61.66m while Tunks took home the silver medal with 60.67m.

The conditions looked tough as throwers were struggling generally. Seema couldn’t get going and her first throw hit the frame of the shot put area.

World.title: Figuratively, Dubai 15th district of Kerala, says Brittas as JDU MP alleges ‘foreign role’ in Jantar Mantar stir
World.content:
JD(U) MP Sanjay Kumar Jha on Thursday alleged foreign involvement in the Jantar Mantar agitation, triggering protests from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha.

Participating in a discussion on the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, Jha said while the Cockroach Janata Party protests were underway, he had seen a Malayalam television channel reporting that “some Dubai-based businessmen had secured travel tickets for 23 people and helped them participate in the protests”.

“What relation did these people have with NEET? The demand of students and their sentiments are genuine. But it is a matter of investigation as to who were the people who infiltrated the protest and were trying to hijack it,” Jha said.

The remarks immediately sparked protests from the Opposition benches, led by MPs from Kerala, who sought to rebut the allegation. The Chair, however, did not permit interventions as Jha was still speaking.

Later, CPI(M) MP A A Rahim said Jha should authenticate his statement about watching a Malayalam channel, arguing that his allegations were not supported by facts. The Chair said it would examine the matter.



CPI(M) member John Brittas argued that those who had travelled from Dubai were Indian citizens and had every right to participate in protests.

“They are citizens of India. Figuratively, Dubai is the 15th district of Kerala. They have every right to come to India and participate in a protest. A wrong message should not go from this House,” Brittas said.

Responding to the controversy over Sanjeev Mukhiya, whom the CBI gave a clean chit in the 2024 NEET paper leak case last year, Jha said Mukhiya remained lodged in Buxar jail in connection with other criminal cases. “There are so many cases against him that there is no possibility of him getting out,” he said.



The issue of Mukhiya, who was initially arrested by Bihar Police in the 2024 NEET paper leak case and later taken into custody by the CBI, had been raised earlier in the debate by Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge.

Jha appealed to the members to rise above partisan politics while discussing exam paper leaks. “When a question paper is leaked, it does not merely violate the secrecy of the exam but also erodes the trust in the system… So I request that this issue not be measured on the yardstick of politics. The students are not asking who belongs to which party. She is asking if her hard work is secure and if she will get justice. Parliament has to answer this question,” he said.



Calling paper leaks a recurring national problem, Jha said: “Paper leak is not a new issue. In different times, under governments of different parties, such issues have come up. The biggest cost of this is paid by students. This is not a question of the failure of a party or government; it is a national challenge. Its solution should be found with a national perspective.”

World.title: After 12 years, India completes first comprehensive catalogue of butterflies, moths
World.content:
India’s Lepidoptera diversity now stands at 3,705 genera, 240 subfamilies, 102 families and 31 superfamilies, spanning ecosystems from the Himalayas to the Western Ghats and the tropical forests.

By Antoreep Das

India has completed its first comprehensive national catalogue of butterflies and moths, bringing together more than a century of scattered taxonomic records into a single reference after a 12-year effort led by the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI).

Announced on Thursday, the catalogue documents 13,703 species of Lepidoptera — the insect order comprising butterflies and moths — found across the country. According to the ZSI, the compilation provides the first updated national baseline for biodiversity research, ecological monitoring and conservation planning.

The survey estimates that India is home to 8.25 per cent of the world’s known butterfly and moth species, highlighting the country’s status as one of the world’s megadiverse nations.

World.title: Despite struggling with knee, Tejaswin finishes 1st day of Decathlon at 2nd spot
World.content:
India's Tejaswin Shankar competes in the men's decathlon long jump at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, Thursday, July 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Alastair Grant)

Tejaswin Shankar, India’s national record holder in Decathlon, finished in second position after the end of five events with a total of 4339 points.

Tejaswin, who earlier retired from the men’s high jump due to a knee injury, started the Decathlon with a 10.96s timing in the 100m and accumulated 870 points.

He was placed seventh after the fifth event.

Despite struggling with his knee, Tejaswin produced a big personal best in the long jump to record 7.82m and improve his previous personal best of 7.67m. He gained 1015 points for the effort placing him at the second spot.

In the shot put, he again came up with an average show recording a best throw of 13.09m in his three attempts to finish the event in seventh place. The effort earned him 673 points, which further dropped him to 5th place in the overall standings after three events, with a total of 2,558 points.

World.title: 9 died in March 18 blaze: Bronto Skylift failed, crew not trained — magisterial inquiry report on Palam fire
World.content:
Bronto Skylift (hydraulic crane) of the Delhi Fire Services (DFS) failed during the rescue operation after its boom became entangled in overhead cables and banners, no backup high-reach rescue equipment was available and firefighters had to rely on a manual ladder that could not reach the third floor balcony – these are the major findings of a magisterial inquiry into the March 18 fire in a four-story building in Palam that killed nine people, including three children, The Indian Express has learnt.

The report was submitted by District Magistrate (South West) Mekala Chaitanya Prasad to the Home department last month. The file is now proposed to be placed before the Lieutenant Governor for consideration, officials said.

“The Bronto Skylift (BS-III) failed at the scene – most likely due to cables/wires/banners entangled in its boom and no effective second line of defence (an alternative tall ladder) was immediately available… a manual ladder could not reach the third-floor balcony,” the report said.

The inquiry also found that the crew assigned to operate the skylift had never received formal training from the authorised dealer since the machine was procured in 2006. “They learned informally from predecessors,” the report said.

It added that maintenance logs of the skylift shows no prior faults were reported despite it being used in operations at IGI Airport, Tilak Nagar and Palam during incidents of fire.

Further, the report highlighted several lapses by the MCD and other agencies, which resulted in the tragedy.

It blamed the MCD for allowing commercial activity on the building’s first floor though the licence permitted commercial use only in the basement and ground floor.



As per the report, the fire probably originated from an MCB box located on the ground and first floor stairs, a point where around six electrical connections were concentrated. It added that the fire “spread rapidly, aggravated by combustible cosmetic stock”.

While a short circuit is considered the probable cause of the fire, the report said this cannot be confirmed until the forensic report is received because the electrical installation was extensively damaged.

The report recommended disciplinary action against MCD licensing inspector Narendra Dabas for failing to check violation of license conditions. “Dabas, who was working under the supervision of assistant commissioner Najafgarh Zone also failed in his duty for removal of aerial banners on roads,” it added.

According to the report, firefighters had to manually clear low-hanging cables and banners with the help of local residents before positioning the Bronto Skylift, delaying rescue efforts.



It also flagged that the assistant electrical inspector, who led the inspection, had received no technical training since he joined the Fire department in 2012. “…admitted he had never been able to determine the cause of fire in any of 8-9 prior inspections – a serious capability gap in a statutory technical role,” the report highlighted.

It recommended that a technical expert committee be set up to investigate the Bronto Skylift’s failure, ensure deployment of backup high-rise rescue equipment at major fires and filling up of 853 vacant posts in the Fire department on priority.

Highlighting that the fire could not be controlled due to “unauthorised cabling” in the area by cable and Internet service providers, the report recommended: “Bring all local cable/Internet service providers under a regulatory framework… Make provider name-marking on cables compulsory for identification of violators, consider road width as a criterion (while deciding on installing) overhead (or) underground cabling. Initiate penal action against the operators identified… and any others found culpable.”

On structural safety, the report called for installing mobile-linked fire alarms in shops, retrofitting of windows and balconies, and stricter enforcement of unified building bye-laws.

World.title: Likely before fast-track court: Paper leak cases impacted after judge was moved out at key stages
World.content:
The fast-track court of Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga will take up the CBI’s 20,000-page chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case on Monday.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the setting up of fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for exam fraud in the midst of the students’ protest demanding accountability for the NEET leak.

Besides the NEET case, Judge Baliga’s court is also likely to take up other exam fraud cases.

Here are three cases which had come before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Neetu Nagar of Rouse Avenue Courts before the judge was deputed to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) last month.

2003 CAT paper leak

STATUS : Still at the stage of “arguments on charge” before a Rouse Avenue Magistrate Court. This is the stage before the framing of charges. Trials start only after charges have been framed by the court.

AFFECTED CANDIDATES: More than 1.25 lakh candidates had applied for the Common Admission Test scheduled for November 23, 2003. The test was cancelled, and held in February 2004.



WHAT HAPPENED: On November 22, a day before the exam, the Delhi Police was tipped off that the paper had been leaked. The CBI, which took over the investigation, zeroed in on a hotel in Mahipalpur in south-west Delhi, where it seized various sections of the alleged question paper from individuals in two rooms.

Investigators recorded the statements of candidates who claimed that Rs 2 lakh to Rs 4 lakh had been demanded from them for the “leaked paper”.

The CBI submitted the chargesheet in 2004.

PROGRESS OF CASE : From May 2019, when the case was transferred to the Rouse Avenue Court, to May 2026, there were nine hearings every year on average. The Covid-19 pandemic contributed to the delay.

On June 3 this year, ACJM Nagar reserved her order on the charges due to the “heavy cause list” and because “no time was left”. The ACJM said the order would be passed on June 26.



However, on June 22, she was deputed to the NGT’s Principal Bench in New Delhi, where she is currently Deputy Registrar. The 2003 case is now before a ‘link’ judge, who is also a Magistrate at the Rouse Avenue Court.

2023 AIIMS NORCET-4 leak

STATUS: Arguments on charge were heard for about a year, but not completed. They will now be heard afresh by the fast-track court.

AFFECTED CANDIDATES: Around 90,000.

WHAT HAPPENED : The exam to recruit nurses in AIIMS and four other hospitals in Delhi was held on June 3, 2023. Two days after the exam, a leak was alleged on social media. Screenshots, allegedly of a candidate’s console, were posted.

On June 6, the Associate Dean (Exams) of AIIMS filed a complaint against one Ritu, and Gian Jyoti Institute of Management and Technology, Phase-II, Mohali. The CBI registered an FIR alleging that a computer at the institute was used by or on behalf of Ritu for the “purpose of cheating”.



The CBI alleged a criminal conspiracy to “rig the examination process by using unfair means in favour of accused candidates against illegal monetary consideration”. It claimed that the accused persons had informed others that they “would get the answers before 30 minutes of completion of the examination”.

PROGRESS OF CASE: On August 28, 2023, Magistrate Deepak Kumar 2 took cognizance of the chargesheet. Later, the case came to ACJM Nagar, who had replaced Kumar.

ACJM Nagar was hearing arguments on charge when she was deputed to the NGT last month. She last heard arguments on June 9.

2024 UGC NET paper leak

STATUS: CBI has filed a closure report, which the court has refused to accept.

AFFECTED CANDIDATES: The alleged leak impacted more than 9 lakh candidates who appeared for the exam in 317 cities.



WHAT HAPPENED: The eligibility exam for entry-level teaching jobs in colleges and admission to PhD courses was held on June 18, 2024. On June 19, the Education Ministry cancelled the exam after “inputs from National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit of Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)…prima facie indicate[d] that the integrity of the…examination may have been compromised”.

In July, the CBI found that the alleged evidence on which the Education Ministry had acted was “doctored”. This alleged “evidence” was a purported screenshot of the paper that was circulated on Telegram around 2 pm on the day of the exam, with messages and comments suggesting the paper had been leaked before the first session of the exam.

PROGRESS OF CASE: The CBI filed a closure report in January 2025, saying it had found no evidence of a leak. It said that forensic experts had established that the purported screenshot was created by a school student using a mobile phone application.



After the report was filed, 13 hearings were held. On May 15, 2026, ACJM Nagar asked CBI to explain in writing why it had filed a closure report even though its own findings showed that a suspect had collected money from candidates by “luring them with leaked question papers”.

The explanation furnished by the investigating officer is yet to be considered by the court. After ACJM Nagar was deputed to NGT, the case was heard once by a link judge. The next date of hearing is August 6.

World.title: Love, lies and fake gold: An extramarital affair that led to a Rs 3-crore loan fraud
World.content:
Pankaj was arrested on July 7. Bansal is out on bail.

It began with a phone call received from a wrong number.

Around 2015, Pankaj Kumar, a gold appraiser at non-banking financial company (NBFC) Sai Corporation in Delhi, received a call from a woman who had dialled the wrong number. The two stayed in touch and eventually began an affair.

Pankaj, however, was already married with two children. He soon found out that it was difficult to support both his family and the woman on his salary.

The result: he went on to siphon money from his company, orchestrating a gold loan fraud worth more than Rs 3 crore over six years.

During this time, he transferred around Rs 90 lakh to bank accounts linked to the woman in multiple transactions.

World.title: Eye on 800 TPD waste management, MCD signs deal with Oil India to set up CBG plants
World.content:
According to MCD sources, an agreement with Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services (IL&FS) to operate a 300 TDP CBG plant at Okhla landfill site was called off before the deal with OIL was signed.

To convert 800 tonnes per day (TPD) of wet waste into biogas and organic fertilizers, the Municipal Corporation Delhi (MCD) and the Oil India Limited (OIL) on Thursday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in the presence of the Delhi CM Rekha Gupta and Mayor Pravesh Wahi for the establishment of two Bio-Methanation based Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) plants, officials said.

According to an official statement, two Bio-CBG plants with a combined processing capacity of 800 TPD will be established in the first phase. A 500 TPD plant will be developed on 10 acres of land at Tehkhand, while a 300 TPD plant will be set up on 7 acres at Okhla, an official said. These facilities will scientifically process segregated organic waste to produce CBG and organic fertilizer, contributing to cleaner and more sustainable waste management, the official added.

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs1.09, HSD price by Rs2.42
World.content:
The government on Thursday increased the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.09 and Rs2.42 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.15 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs393.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 31 (Friday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Naqvi urges 'all political parties' to settle issue of more provinces, says current 'system' has collapsed
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday urged all political parties to “settle” various national-level issues, including the question of creating new provinces.

Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 being held in Islamabad, Naqvi said there was “only one solution” to improving the country’s overall condition: “You will have to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public.”

The interior minister argued: “All political parties should sit together in a single room, whether for a day, a month or a year. They will have to settle every issue of their country, including new units and provinces.”

“Unless they do so, unless they sit together and change this, this country will remain in the same condition, regardless of how many seminars and functions you hold.”

Various political parties have demanded the creation of more provinces or administrative units for better governance.

The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh.

However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move.

On the other hand, the PPP and the PTI have long advocated for a South Punjab province.

At the outset of his speech, Naqvi said, “Whether you agree or not, the system we have been living under has collapsed.”

He contended that there would be no change in the country’s conditions if the same “system” remains.

The minister emphasised that ordinary citizens wanted to be able to afford necessities and have interactions with the government, which were not being provided.

He further said: “The condition of this federal government is such that we make our budgets in the negative, and we discuss how much debt we have to incur this year.”

“[…] We will take more debts, but we will not correct things,” he pointed out.

Asserting that he was the “biggest supporter” of democracy, Naqvi highlighted that there were multiple systems even within democracy. “But we say, no matter what, we have to keep running and dragging this,” he added.

The minister said Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts, which were even hailed globally, were “simply firefighting”. “Until you correct the basics of this country while adhering to the spirit of democracy, this will remain the same,” he said.

Noting that Islamabad was a “very busy city”, Naqvi said, “Unless units are made and they take ownership, and a new leadership comes, this will not happen.”

He went on to remark that giving “stipends and tablets to youngsters” would not make them happy, as the youth wanted merit-based job opportunities and a “corrected system”.

“We are not able to give the youth that,” the interior minister said.

“If these ‘cockroaches’ get united, they can turn everything upside down,” he quipped, referring to a term often used for Gen-Z in the wake of recent student protests in India.

Noting that all business chambers and associations were present at the summit, the minister said he considered them to be “those who run the political system” and fund it.

“One gives funding of Rs500 million before elections, or the other gives Rs100m or Rs50m.”

He also said that those attending the summit were “responsible for the current state of Pakistan and where it is today”, noting that certain systems had not worked for the past 70 years.

World.title: Gangster Uzair Baloch’s brother shot, critically injured in Karachi’s Lyari: police
World.content:
KARACHI: The brother of imprisoned Uzair Baloch, chief of the defunct People’s Amn Committee, was shot and critically wounded in Karachi’s Lyari area on Thursday evening, according to police.

Chakiwara police, in a statement, said that Zubair Baloch, 40, was shot and injured on main Chakiwara Road, while two passersby were also injured. They were shifted to Civil Hospital Karachi.

South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that Zubair had been arrested in seven criminal cases in 2012 and was released in January 2025.

He added that Zubair was sitting outside his residence in Singu Lane when armed suspects on a motorcycle opened fire on him and fled the scene.

Zubair sustained multiple injuries, including to his chest and abdomen, and was undergoing surgery. DIG Raza noted that one of the injured passersby was also in serious condition.

The DIG added that the police were investigating the incident from different angles, including gang rivalry and personal enmity.

A social activist from the area told Dawn, on the condition of anonymity, that Zubair had joined a “political party” a few months ago and had raised its flags in his area.

The activist also mentioned rumours in Lyari that some gangsters who had fled to Dubai and Iran after the Karachi operation had returned following the US-Iran war, and that residents were fearful of a possible resurgence of the past gang war in the area.

They added that the attackers had covered their faces and fled when a nearby shopkeeper returned fire.

Earlier in March, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected bail applications of Uzair Baloch in seven cases pertaining to murder, police encounter and possession of explosives.

Uzair, along with others, had been charged with attacking law enforcers with firearms and explosives in 2012 within the jurisdiction of the Kalakot police station.

World.title: Renewed Middle East tensions pose downside risks to inflation, external sector: finance ministry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Anticipating the new fiscal year to begin with double-digit inflation, the government on Thursday expressed concern over renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, saying they posed downside risks to inflation and the external outlook.

“Renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pose downside risks to inflation and the external outlook,” the Ministry of Finance said in its Monthly Economic Update & Outlook (July 2026), while assuring that the external sector would remain resilient, supported by government measures to facilitate exports and sustain the strong momentum in remittance inflows.

“Overall, prudent macroeconomic management, fiscal discipline, ongoing structural reforms, stronger industrial activity and improved external buffers are expected to sustain the recovery in economic activity while preserving macroeconomic stability,” the finance ministry said, adding that macroeconomic stabilisation had largely been achieved in FY2026.

It said the economy was expected to maintain its growth momentum in the current fiscal year, supported by “improving macroeconomic fundamentals, continued expansion in the manufacturing sector, fiscal consolidation, resilience in agriculture and a stable financial environment”.

Manufacturing activity was likely to maintain its positive trajectory, underpinned by stable energy availability, easing financial conditions, improving domestic demand and continued export-oriented production, the ministry said.

“Inflation, however, is expected to remain elevated in the near term, with CPI inflation projected in the range of 9-10 per cent in July 2026.”

At the same time, it also warned that normalisation of global energy prices remained contingent on a durable and lasting peace agreement between the US and Iran.

Among high-frequency indicators, the US Weekly Economic Index (WEI), which measures real-time economic activity, stood at 2.9pc for the week ended July 18, while its 13-week moving average stood at 2.87pc.

Likewise, the ministry said the Composite Leading Indicator suggested that Pakistan’s major export markets (OECD economies such as the UK and the US) remained broadly aligned with their long-term potential of 100, indicating continued support from external demand, although renewed geopolitical tensions could pose downside risks.

The ministry said the government’s focus on poverty alleviation and social protection continued during the fiscal year that had just ended.

In June 2026, the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment registered 38,410 workers for overseas employment, reflecting continued opportunities for Pakistani workers in international labour markets, it said.

The finance ministry noted that Pakistan’s economy entered FY2027 with an improved macroeconomic environment, as the stabilisation gains of FY2026 continued to support economic recovery and strengthen prospects for sustainable growth.

“In FY2026, average CPI inflation remained within the targeted range despite elevated global oil prices and supply chain disruptions.

“Large-scale manufacturing rebounded and agriculture maintained moderate growth despite weather-related challenges.

“Improved revenue mobilisation and prudent expenditure management further strengthened the fiscal position. The external sector remained broadly balanced, with the current account recording a marginal deficit of $140 million. Record-high workers’ remittances and higher foreign exchange reserves helped offset the import recovery associated with the strengthening of domestic economic activity.”

Meanwhile, it said IT exports reached a record $4.6 billion (up 20.6pc from last year), underscoring Pakistan’s growing potential in technology and digital services. Keeping in view these positive developments, S&P Global Ratings recently upgraded Pakistan’s long-term sovereign credit rating to B from B-, indicating improved institutional capacity, sustained implementation of reforms, improved fiscal performance and a significant rebuilding of foreign exchange reserves.

“With these gains continuing to advance the foundations for sustained economic growth, real GDP growth is targeted at 4pc in FY2027, based on the government’s continued advancement of the reform agenda through deepening financial markets, broadening the domestic investor base, strengthening debt sustainability and enhancing the country’s presence in the global capital market,” the ministry said.

Nevertheless, it warned that renewed US-Iran hostilities once again posed downside risks through global energy prices, trade and financial market volatility.

However, stronger macroeconomic fundamentals, improved external buffers, government readiness and continued policy vigilance have enhanced Pakistan’s capacity to manage such shocks effectively, the ministry concluded.

World.title: ECP refuses to recognise Achakzai as PkMAP chief over failure to hold intra-party polls
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday refused to recognise National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai as chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) over the party’s failure to hold intra-party elections.

A full five-member bench of the commission, headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, heard the matter.

Two other cases related to the party were also fixed for hearing. It was learnt that not only Achakzai’s leadership but also certain “controversial” amendments made to the party’s constitution and PkMAP’s account details were under question.

At the initial hearing last week, the ECP bench had observed that a decision would first be made regarding the party’s counsel, Aimal Mandokhail. On Thursday, the chief election commissioner said an order would be issued regarding the power of attorney.

Raja made the remarks after asking the lawyer who had signed the power of attorney submitted to the commission.

Mandokhail replied that party chairman Achakzai had signed the document, but the chief election commissioner pointed out that there was currently no party head, as no intra-party election had been conducted so far.

He added that the power of attorney would be placed on record, but an order would be issued on whether or not it was acceptable.

Mandokhail has sought to represent the party in the three cases, but this is now subject to the ECP’s order on the power of attorney.

It was learnt that PkMAP had conducted intra-party elections on December 21, 2022, and since the term of office-bearers was fixed at three years, new elections were mandatory by December 21, 2025.

Raja said the commission had reminded the party to hold elections on October 1, 2025, and issued a show-cause notice on January 15, 2026. In response, the party sought a 180-day extension, which was granted.

However, a subsequent request for another 180-day extension was rejected, with the commission clarifying that intra-party elections must be completed by June 19, 2026, in any case. The party neither held the elections nor submitted a proper response to the ECP.

World.title: PM Shehbaz briefed on digitisation of consular services for overseas Pakistanis: PMO
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The foreign ministry briefed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on enhanced consular services for overseas Pakistanis, including the digitisation of systems for services such as document attestation and foreign payments, the PMO said on Thursday.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, PM Shehbaz chaired a meeting in Islamabad, where he was briefed on the progress of these initiatives by officials from the foreign ministry, the interior ministry, the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), the IT ministry, Pakistan’s ambassadors posted in various countries and other senior officials.

The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, alongside Federal Ministers Ahsan Iqbal Cheema, Attaullah Tarar, Chaudhry Salik Hussain and Shaza Fatima Khawaja; Minister of State Aoun Chaudhry, Special Assistant Tariq Bajwa, and other senior officials.

The briefing covered enhanced services at Pakistani embassies for overseas Pakistanis, the digitisation of the document attestation process, a further simplified mechanism for complaints, and the introduction of digital systems for various services, as well as payments to Pakistan from abroad, the statement said.

“Overseas Pakistanis are our valuable asset, and providing them with all kinds of facilities is the government’s top priority,” it quoted the prime minister as saying.

The meeting was informed that, for the convenience of overseas Pakistanis, a QR code-based system has already been introduced to simplify the processes regarding the power of attorney, purchase and sale of property, and attestation of documents.

The prime minister welcomed the digitisation of the complaints registration system through QR codes, directing that these codes be prominently displayed at Pakistani embassies and missions abroad to improve public access.

He instructed that a special awareness campaign be launched for overseas Pakistanis so that a greater number of people would be able to use the QR code-based system to register their complaints.

The meeting was informed that an evening shift has recently been launched at the Foreign Office in Islamabad to facilitate citizens. Document attestation services have also been introduced at the Asaan Khidmat Centre in Islamabad.

Alongside the launch of a courier-based document attestation service, the system has also been integrated with the databases of the Higher Education Commission (HEC), Inter Boards Coordination Commission, the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra), and the National Police Bureau, making the attestation process faster and more efficient”, according to the PMO statement.

The participants were further informed that the attestation process has been converted into a one-step procedure under the Apostille system — which reduces the process to the issuance of one authentication certificate, an “Apostille”, by the designated authority of the country where the document was issued.

The premier was informed that work was progressing rapidly on the next phase to fully digitise this entire system.

With the support of the National Information Technology Board (NITB), a mobile application is being developed through which documents such as birth and death certificates, marriage registration certificates, family registration certificates, and other official documents will also be digitally attested, the statement said.

The briefing followed an earlier meeting at the foreign ministry, chaired by DPM Dar, to review measures for further improving consular services.

Dar was briefed on the “steps undertaken to enhance public facilitation, including plans to digitalise consular services, and the introduction of morning and evening shifts to provide greater accessibility and convenience to citizens,” the FO said on X.

He directed that these services be further strengthened to ensure “efficient, transparent, and timely facilitation” for the public.

In May, the deputy premier highlighted the country’s economic progress and inviting overseas Pakistanis to “honour their roots” and invest in the country, while addressing Pakistani-American community leaders in New York.

World.title: Bilawal warns ‘countdown’ will begin for federal government if it 'steals' AJK election
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned on Thursday that a stolen election in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) would start a “countdown” for the federal government.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on Monday. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

“The PML-N thinks that after its defeat in Gilgit-Baltistan, a defeat in AJK would mean a countdown begins for its government,” Bilawal said while addressing a rally in Muzaffarabad ahead of the August 2 elections. “But this is a misconception.”

“If you steal [the election] … write it down, take my guarantee, that a countdown will start for your federal government,” he warned. “If you steal my mandate, I will come for your throne.”

The PPP scion added that his party had elders who had challenged former leaders, including General Ziaul Haq and Pervez Musharraf, and were experts at “hunting lions”.

He also extended a message to the PTI — which has rejected the AJK elections over alleged rigging concerns — to “start doing politics” and leave behind “boycott politics”.

“Boycotting elections, boycotting Parliament, boycotting committees, boycotting your work, boycotting struggle — if you want to boycott, you might as well just sit at home,” he said, calling on the PTI to contest the elections and conduct themselves as a political party.

“Today I extend my hand towards PTI’s workers, towards its serious politicians,” he said. “To every political party that is tired of rigging, to every political worker who wants to make their own decision, come and join your hands with mine.”

He expressed hope that together they could bring about parliamentary reforms and ensure fair elections in Kashmir and across Pakistan, saying he was ready to work with all political parties on that agenda.

Bilawal added that there was one way to stop rigging in an election: to turn out in such large numbers that an “injection” of false votes would not be effective. He called on PPP supporters to ensure such massive turnout during the second phase of the elections on August 2.

While addressing the rally, he said he welcomed the PML-N’s promise to provide buses to Kashmir, but added: “If you come to Muzaffarabad bringing the spectacle of what you have done in Lahore, people will ask: what have you done in Muzaffarabad?”

Referring to the CMH flyover project in AJK, he pointed out that it had not been completed in five years. Meanwhile, the PPP was responsible for the construction of all three medical colleges in Kashmir as well as the construction of universities.

“I don’t want to make Kashmir into Punjab, or even Sindh,” the PPP chairman said. “I want … to make Kashmir into a strong Kashmir. I want to see it free.”

Bilawal said that the first task for the elected government would be to end the difficulties faced by the people of AJK, including opening roads, delivering essential supplies and restoring internet and banking services. He highlighted that the PPP wanted to bring “fast, modern” internet to the region to allow it to stay connected.

Throughout his address, he stressed his commitment to Kashmir’s right to make decisions regarding its own future, votes and resources, as well as jobs for its youth.

He restated his intention to deliver “sovereignty, ownership and employment” to the people of AJK, saying that in institutions of Pakistan where decisions were made on Kashmir’s “water, electricity, economy, budget and future”, Kashmir should have rightful representation and its own voice.

“Election decisions should be done by ballots, not bullets. Votes should be counted during the election, not bodies,” he said.

Recalling that Benazir Bhutto had given Kashmiris observer status at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, he pledged to also deliver observer status to Kashmiris in the National Finance Commission, Council of Common Interests, National Assembly and Senate.

Bilawal also stated his intention to deliver the same sovereignty and ownership to refugees, calling them “a part of our existence, our history and our movement”. He called for their rightful proportional representation in the AJK Assembly to be protected.

He stressed that Kashmiri citizens were the “real owners” of the region’s natural resources, calling for the protection of their rivers and environment and for the region to receive a fair financial share for the use of its resources. He added that the first right to jobs created through projects in the region should go to its own youth.

The PPP chairman stressed that the PPP had submitted proof of winning 90-100 per cent of votes in Mirpur to the AJK Election Commission, but regretted that a notification had been issued instead.

“I want to ask the election commissioner: are you an election commissioner for the PML-N, or the state of AJK?” he said, adding that a notification could not hide theft or stop justice. He demanded that ahead of August 2, complaints regarding the first phase of elections be heard publicly, and polling station results and ballot counts be brought before the public.

“If it is not theft, then what are you hiding?” he emphasised, calling on the commission to restore its credibility.

World.title: Arshad Nadeem qualifies for javelin throw final at Commonwealth Games
World.content:
Pakistani Olympic gold medallist Arshad Nadeem cleared the qualifying round in the men’s javelin throw on Monday, the seventh day of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, with a seasonal best score.

The 29-year-old Arshad, who won the javelin throw gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham with a record throw of 90.18 metres, is participating in the 2026 Games being held in Scotland from July 23-Aug 2.

The qualifying round, which was held earlier today, saw Arshad throw his season’s best of 78.63 metres, securing his spot in the final event in seventh place.

The men’s javelin throw final will be held tomorrow (Friday) from 6:30pm to 10:15pm local time (10:30pm to 2:15am PKT).

Last year, Arshad was named the Global Breakthrough Athlete at the Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Sports Awards during the World Sports Summit in December.

However, he made an underwhelming return to competition earlier this month ahead of the Glasgow games, finishing ninth in the javelin throw at the Spitzen Leicht­athletik Luzern meeting in Switzerland on July 16.

Competing in the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver event, his best effort was 78.47 metres, recorded with his final throw. His series read: X, 74.87m, 73.26m, X, 73.39m and 78.47m.

Speaking after his final training session at the Punjab Stadium in Lahore before departing for both events, Arshad said he had prepared well for the Commonwealth Games.

However, he faces tough competition in the Glasgow final, with India’s Neeraj Chopra and Rohit Yadav, as well as Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga, qualifying alongside him. Tharanga currently sits atop today’s rankings with an 82.84m throw.

The top 15 scorers in the men’s javelin throw qualifying round at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland on July 30, with Arshad Nadeem ranking seventh. — screengrab via glasgow2026.com

Also competing in the event was Muhammad Yasir, who threw his season’s best of 74.36m but failed to make the top 12 qualifiers, finishing in 14th place.

At last year’s Asian Throwing Championships, the Yasir threw a massive 77.43m on his sixth and final attempt, snagging a bronze medal and smashing his previous season’s best.

In his comments earlier this month, Arshad recalled memories of the 2022 Commonwealth Games and acknowledged the pressure he felt to live up to his accolades.

“Four years after I broke the Commonwealth Games record in 2022, I remain in the same position,” the star athlete said. “There is also pressure [on me] … I have been the champion for four years and now I will need to again do well [to retain the title].”

“There is always pressure while entering the field … that pressure has to be controlled.”
